title: Synthesis of Enones and Enals From Alkenes via Alkenyl Thianthrenium Salts
source: Angewandte Chemie International Edition
abstract: ABSTRACT Herein, we show the stereoselective conversion of alkenes into enones and enals. Alkenyl thianthrenium salts are used as a readily accessible pool of stereodefined alkenyl electrophiles that can be engaged in two types of carbonylative Pd‐catalyzed three‐component coupling reactions. Using alkyl zinc species generated in situ from alkyl iodides, enones can be accessed via a carbonylative Negishi coupling. In the presence of triethylsilane, enals can be generated via reductive carbonylation.

title: Frontispiece: Isolated Ir–Se Sites in Nickel Selenide for Glyoxal‐Mediated Ethylene Glycol Oxidation to Formate and PET Upcycling
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: Sustainable upcycling of polyethylene terephthalate to formate requires catalysts that selectively drive the electrochemical oxidation pathways of ethylene glycol. In Research Article e6834878, Myong Yong Choi and co-workers show that the Se-coordinated Ir sites in NiSe modulate the electronic structure of neighboring Ni sites, promoting surface reconstruction to active NiOOH. The resulting catalyst enables glyoxal-mediated oxidation of ethylene glycol to formate and efficient PET upcycling.

title: Engineering Amino‐Induced p‐π Conjugation for Electronic Regulation of Li + Transport in PVDF‐Based Solid‐State Electrolytes
source: Angewandte Chemie International Edition
abstract: ABSTRACT Sluggish Li + transport in poly(vinylidene fluoride) (PVDF)‐based solid polymer electrolytes (SPEs) arises from restricted polymer segmental motion and persistent Li + ‐FSI − association, while conventional fillers provide limited regulation of the local electronic and coordination environments. Herein, amino‐functionalized UiO66‐NH 2 is introduced into a PVDF/lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide (LiFSI) electrolyte to construct electronically active composite SPEs (U6NP). The electron‐donating ─NH 2 groups induce p‐π conjugation, redistribute the linker electron density, and strengthen ligand‐to‐metal charge transfer (LMCT)‐related electronic coupling between the organic linkers and Zr‐O clusters. This electronic reconstruction, together with amino‐associated modulation of local O‐centered coordination environments, reshapes the electrostatic landscape, weakens Li + ‐FSI − interactions, and facilitates Li + migration. U6NP delivers a room‐temperature ionic conductivity of 2.41 × 10 −3 S cm −1 , a Li + transference number of 0.56, and an oxidative stability of 4.42 V. More importantly, Li||U6NP||LiNi 0.8 Co 0.1 Mn 0.1 O 2 (NCM811) cells with a cathode loading of 21.5 mg cm −2 retain 98.51% after 120 cycles at 0.05 C. The Li||U6NP||NCM811 pouch cell delivers 136.6 mAh g −1 initially and 120.9 mAh g −1 after 100 cycles. This work establishes ─NH 2 ‐induced p‐π conjugation‐enhanced LMCT as an effective strategy for electronically active MOF‐reinforced PVDF electrolytes toward high‐loading solid‐state lithium metal batteries.

title: Reconfiguring Interfacial Electrochemical Potential for Boosting Sodium‐Ion Transport in Composite Solid Electrolytes
source: Angewandte Chemie International Edition
abstract: ABSTRACT Sluggish ion transport kinetics between the ceramic and polymer phases remain a key challenge in composite solid electrolytes (CSEs), primarily due to a severe interfacial barrier arising from their intrinsic physicochemical incompatibility. Herein, molecular design‐enabled electronic structure engineering is proposed to reconfigure the interfacial electrochemical environment at the Na 3 Zr 2 Si 2 PO 12 –poly(ethylene oxide) interface, based on a dual‐axis screening guided by the electron‐donating capability and molecular electronic asymmetry. By grafting different functional trimethoxysilanes from a targeted library onto the ceramic surface, the effect of the interfacial electrochemical potential on Na‐ion transport is investigated, revealing a strong negative correlation with the ionic conductivity of CSEs. The CSE with the optimal grafting molecule (phenyltrimethoxysilane) reduces the potential mismatch by 87% and lowers the Na‐ion migration barrier, thereby boosting Na‐ion conductivity by two orders of magnitude. All‐solid‐state sodium‐metal batteries using this CSE show boosted electrochemical performance with a high capacity of 91.8 mAh g −1 delivered at 5 C and retain ∼99% of their initial capacity after 500 cycles at 2 C. This work establishes a screening framework for reducing interfacial potential mismatch and addressing the long‐standing ion‐transport bottleneck across ceramic–polymer interfaces in CSEs.

title: Photocatalytic 1,2‐Boron Migrative Alkene Homologation to Access 1,3‐Difunctionalized Alkenes
source: Angewandte Chemie International Edition
abstract: ABSTRACT In contrast to well‐established methods for vicinal di‐functionalization of alkenes, remote di‐functionalization is much more challenging and has achieved limited success. Herein, we disclose a visible light photocatalytic boron‐directed alkene homologation with alkyl halides activated by a traceless tert ‐butylsulfonyl (Bus) leaving group. The reaction produces a myriad of 1,3‐difunctionalized alkenes under mild conditions with excellent functional group tolerance. β‐Elimination of the Bus group not only drives the contra‐thermodynamic 1,2‐boron migration, but also regenerates a C─C double bond, thus transforming the sulfone‐based alkyl halide into a vinylidene precursor, rather than a traditional alkyl source. The synthetic utility of this method is well demonstrated by gram‐scale synthesis, downstream transformations, and the formal total synthesis of 24‐fluoro‐25‐hydroxyvitamin D 3 analogues. This work represents a very rare example of one‐carbon homologation of ubiquitous alkenes, thus establishing a new strategic paradigm for chemical synthesis.

title: A Scalable Presodiation Strategy Enabling Dry‐Air‐Processable Hard Carbon Anodes for High Energy Sodium‐Ion Batteries
source: Angewandte Chemie International Edition
abstract: ABSTRACT Hard carbon (HC) anodes hold promise for sodium‐ion batteries but are plagued by low initial Coulombic efficiency (ICE) stemming from irreversible sodium sequestration. Chemical presodiation offers a direct route to compensate this deficit, yet its translation to high‐loading electrodes is crippled by sluggish mass transport and air sensitivity of the sodiated product, a barrier to scalable manufacturing. Here, we break this impasse by synchronizing acoustic field enhanced transport with in situ interfacial engineering. Ultrasound‐driven microconvection and cavitation overcome diffusion limitations within thick electrodes, delivering ∼100% ICE within one minute, approximately twice as fast as conventional immersion. A five second quenching in sodium difluoro(oxalato)borate constructs a B/F‐rich hybrid interphase that not only passivates the highly reactive sodiated surface against dry‐air degradation, retaining >79% ICE after 6 h exposure, but also selfregulates subsequent solid‐electrolyte interphase evolution, suppressing impedance growth and stabilizing charge transfer kinetics. Practical pouch cells deliver 76% capacity retention over 700 cycles at 0.5 C/1 C and exhibit superior wide‐temperature adaptability from −40°C to 55°C. By resolving the coupled bottlenecks of kinetic inhomogeneity and environmental instability, this work establishes a scalable, dry‐air‐compatible presodiation paradigm that bridges the gap between laboratory innovation and industrial battery manufacturing.

title: Irradiation‐Wavelength‐Tuned Stepwise [2+2] Cycloaddition of Indolylphenylpropenone Derivatives as a Platform for Light–Mechanical Energy Conversion
source: Angewandte Chemie International Edition
abstract: ABSTRACT Cyclobutane motifs are widely present in natural products, and [2+2] cycloaddition provides a facile route for synthesizing four‐membered rings. However, controlling the regio‐ and stereo‐selectivity of cycloaddition remains a great challenge. In topo‐photochemical reaction, the prearrangement of the reactant molecules can place the atoms at specific positions in the products. In this work, irradiation‐wavelength‐controlled, stepwise photo‐induced topo‐[2+2] cycloaddition of indolylphenylpropenone derivatives was achieved in crystals. Under blue light, one kind of monocyclobutane was produced via the cycloaddition of the vinyl groups; for ( E )‐1‐(5‐bromo‐1 H ‐indol‐1‐yl)‐3‐(3,5‐difluorophenyl)prop‐2‐en‐1‐one ( PEOBr 5 F 35 ), this process proceeded via a single‐crystal‐to‐single‐crystal transformation. Upon subsequent irradiation with 365 nm light, the monocyclobutane product underwent a second‐step [2+2] cycloaddition between C = C bonds on five‐membered heterocyclic ring in indole, converting into a bicyclobutane product. Such catalyst‐free dearomatization of indole via [2+2] cycloaddition provide a facile and green strategy for constructing cyclobutane‐fused heterocyclic architectures. Driven by [2+2] cycloaddition, the molecular crystals exhibited obvious macroscopic mechanical motion.

title: Universal Thermally‐Driven Non‐Noble Metal Redistribution Strategy Boosts High‐Temperature CO 2 Electrolysis
source: Advanced Materials
abstract: ABSTRACT Efficient and durable CO 2 electrolysis in solid oxide electrolysis cells (SOECs) requires cathodes that integrate high activity with robust stability. Herein, a thermally‐driven non‐noble‐metal redistribution strategy is proposed to overcome the long‐standing limitation in dispersing non‐noble metals on perovskite surfaces, enabling perovskite–ceria composite cathodes with dynamically optimized active sites. Thermal treatment of Cu‐dispersed CeO 2 (Cu 0.05 Ce 0.95 O 2 , 5CC) coupled with Sr 2 Fe 1.5 Mo 0.5 O 6− δ (SFM) induces spontaneous Cu migration and redistribution, which can tailor the electronic structure, increase oxygen vacancies and extend triple‐phase boundaries, thereby enhancing CO 2 adsorption, activation and O 2− /e − transport. As a result, a single cell with 5CC–SFM cathode achieves exceptional current densities of 4.14 A cm −2 at 1.5 V under 850°C, respectively. Owing to strong interaction between the redistributed Cu species and perovskite oxide, the single cell maintains stable catalytic performance for 400 h under harsh high‐temperature CO 2 electrolysis conditions. Moreover, this work demonstrates the extended applicability of 5CC–SFM cathode in reversible solid oxide cells (RSOCs) and establishes the generality and methodological significance of thermally‐driven redistribution in achieving highly dispersed non‐noble‐metal species on oxide supports. These findings offer a general framework for the rational design of next‐generation CeO 2 –containing SOEC cathodes and advanced composite materials.

title: An Interfacial Electron Pump Enhanced Photo‐Assisted CO 2 ‐to‐Bioplastic Microbial Electrosynthesis
source: Advanced Materials
abstract: ABSTRACT Most solar‐ and electrochemical CO 2 ‐utilization strategies still terminate in small‐molecule products, whereas direct access to recoverable carbon products such as bioplastics remains uncommon. Here, we develop a photo‐assisted bioelectrochemical platform by coupling a Shewanella oneidensis MR‐1 bioanode functionalized with Ti 3 C 2 T x MXene quantum dots (MQDs) to a Cupriavidus necator biocathode modified with Ni‐doped carbon dots/poly(diallyldimethylammonium chloride) (Ni‐CDs/PDDA). Cell‐associated MQDs form a conductive and photoactive biointerface, operationally described as an interfacial electron pump, that facilitates lactate‐dependent extracellular electron transfer (EET) under applied anodic bias and adds an illumination‐dependent current contribution. The MQDs‐enabled microbial fuel cell (MFC) delivers a peak power density of 0.82 ± 0.03 mW cm −2 under illumination. In the coupled CO 2 ‐fed system, anodic illumination raises polyhydroxybutyrate (PHB) productivity to 131 mg L −1 d −1 at −0.6 V versus the reversible hydrogen electrode (vs. RHE), approximately 47% above the matched dark value over a 12 h interval. The coupled platform reaches an apparent total‐energy‐to‐PHB efficiency of 3.42% when electrical, incident optical, and lactate‐derived chemical inputs are included. Multiscale analyses support an EET‐coupled interfacial relay involving cytochrome/heme‐associated components within the native EET network. This interface‐to‐synthesis strategy links photo‐assisted microbial electron harvesting to H 2 ‐mediated CO 2 ‐to‐PHB biosynthesis.

title: Self‐Confinement‑Tailored Energy Routing for Superior Thermal‐Adaptive Ln‐MOFs Scintillator
source: Advanced Materials
abstract: ABSTRACT Noncontact radiation monitoring in extreme environments is essential across scientific and industrial fields, driving the development of x‑ray scintillators. Conventional scintillators continue to suffer from inadequate exciton utilization, poor thermal stability, or limited processability. In this study, we propose a self‐confinement strategy to tailor energy routing for constructing superior thermal‐adaptive scintillators. Two lanthanide‐organic frameworks, ZJNU‐1006‐Ln and Ln‐BDC‐F, are rationally designed and synthesized. Compared with the free state of pure ligand or its quasi‐confinement state in Ln‐BDC‐F, ZJNU‐1006‐Ln exhibits a strong molecular self‐confinement state arising from compact ligand packing, thereby enhancing exciton utilization, suppressing nonradiative energy dissipation, and optimizing the energy routing. These features endow ZJNU‐1006‐Ln with superior radio‐luminescent performance, including high light yield (max ∼ 62,000 photons MeV ‒1 ), low detection limit (92.7 nGy air s ‒1 ), and great thermal‐stability (3+ /Eu 3+ doping ratios enables precise localization of radiation‐exposed regions over a broad temperature range, particularly encompassing the Earth surface temperature window. This work highlights the self‐confinement effect as a promising strategy for designing advanced inorganic‐organic scintillators.

title: Topological Regioisomerism Enables Triplet–Triplet Energy‐Transfer for Reversible Dual Delayed Fluorescence–Phosphorescence Multicolor Afterglow
source: Angewandte Chemie International Edition
abstract: ABSTRACT Achieving concurrent thermally activated delayed fluorescence (TADF) and room‐temperature phosphorescence (RTP) afterglow in purely organic systems remains elusive owing to limited control over triplet dynamics, competing decay pathways and unclear operational mechanisms. Reversible TADF/RTP modulation within a single host‐guest system is challenging, hindering advances in color‐ and lifetime‐tunable afterglow materials. To achieve this, we utilized regioisomerism as a structural topology control parameter in a host‐guest platform to modulate triplet‐triplet energy transfer (TTET), enabling the transition from exciplex TADF to dual TADF‐RTP afterglow. The optimized system exhibits TADF‐associated delayed emission with an intensity‐weighted apparent lifetime of 617 ms, along with persistent RTP and ∼6.5‐9.5 s afterglow. Temperature‐dependent modulation of I TADF / I RTP ratio enables reversible cryogenic afterglow color evolution from yellow to orange and red through thermally regulated exciton redistribution.

title: Metalized Carbon Nanotube Films with Boosted Atomic Oxygen Resistance as Electromagnetic Interference Shielding Cladding for Low-Earth-Orbit Space Applications
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Electromagnetic interference (EMI) shielding materials are essential for electronic devices and spacecraft operating in low Earth orbit. Developing materials that combine ultrahigh EMI shielding with mechanical robustness and resistance to extreme space environments remains a critical challenge. Herein, large-area acid-treated carbon nanotube film/aluminum (A-CNTF/Al) composite films are fabricated via acid modification of CNTF, followed by Al deposition as a reinforcing layer. The pristine CNTF shows an electrical conductivity of 4.2 × 104 S/m, which rises to 1.6 × 105 and 6.1 × 105 S/m after acid modification and Al metallization, respectively. The as-prepared A-CNT/Al composite film (14 μm) exhibits an average EMI shielding effectiveness (SE) of 66.2 dB, attaining a high absolute EMI shielding effectiveness (SSE/t) of up to 102,160.49 dB cm2 g–1 across 8.2–12.4 GHz, which ranks among the highest documented metrics for lightweight EMI shielding composite materials. Remarkably, the composite film maintains favorable EMI SE (70.9 dB) at 12.4–40 GHz after atomic oxygen irradiation with a fluence of 4 × 1020 atoms cm–2, verifying its great prospect for long-duration on-orbit service. These results demonstrate that acid-induced surface engineering combined with aluminum metallization significantly enhances the electrical and EMI shielding performance of CNTF, providing lightweight, durable, and highly efficient shielding materials for extreme space environments.

title: Forced displacement is associated with health service delivery disruption beyond the effects of armed conflict
source: Scientific community and society : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Humanitarian emergencies test the resilience of global health systems, yet policy is constrained by limited empirical evidence on the magnitude and timing of service delivery disruptions. Here, we assess the association between measured childhood vaccination—as a proxy for health service delivery—and forced displacement, armed conflict, and natural disasters. Across 193 countries from 2000 to 2023, sudden increases in displaced populations were associated with declines in vaccination coverage of approximately 3 to 6 percentage points, persisting for 2 to 3 years before recovery. Dose-response analyses revealed a nonlinear relationship: coverage fell steeply at low displacement levels and plateaued at extreme exposure. Conflict intensity followed a similar nonlinear pattern that plateaued near 3000 annual battle-related deaths while mortality from natural disasters showed no detectable association with coverage. Displacement’s association was largely independent of armed conflict, indicating that displacement may act as a distinct, additive shock rather than a proxy for violence.

title: Topology-Dependent and Size-Controlled Singlet Oxygen Generation in Porphyrinic Coordination Frameworks for Antifungal Photodynamic Therapy
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Two different coordination materials built with the same starting reagents, 5,10,15,20-tetra(4-pyridyl)porphyrin (H2TPyP) and Zn(NO3)2•6H2O, a nonporous 1D-porphyrin-based coordination polymer (CP) [Zn(TPyP)]n (UDS-4) exhibiting a zig-zag topology, and a porous 3D metal-organic framework (MOF) [Zn2(TPyP)(NO2)2]n (UDS-2), have been prepared in various particle sizes. Both nanosized materials exhibited stronger detected singlet oxygen (1O2(1Δg)) near 1280 nm than their bulk counterparts under the measurement conditions, with nanoUDS-2 giving the strongest signal. We then evaluated whether the enhanced 1O2 generation leads to improved antimicrobial photodynamic therapy (aPDT) efficacy. In vitro assays using Botrytis cinerea revealed growth inhibition thresholds of ∼25 ppm for nanoUDS-2, compared to ∼50 ppm for bulk UDS-2, while UDS-4 and the free base ligand exhibited negligible activity. In contrast, nanoUDS-4 required substantially higher concentrations, with a growth inhibition threshold of 200 ppm. Concurrently, using nanoUDS-2 as the most effective photosensitizer (PS), visible-light treatment of tomatoes and apples markedly suppressed grey mold lesions without detectable damage to the fruit.

title: Molecular Engineering of Customizable Resin-Derived Hard Carbon Framework for Efficient Sodium Storage
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Owing to their high carbon yield and molecular controllability, resins have emerged as promising precursors for hard carbon (HC) anodes in sodium-ion batteries (SIBs). However, achieving synergistic optimization of carbon microcrystals and sub-nanopores during resin pyrolysis to enhance sodium storage capacity remains a significant challenge. Herein, a spatial-chemistry-directed crosslinking (SCDC) strategy, based on the Mannich reaction of selected target molecules (TMs) within a resin network, is proposed. Owing to the steric hindrance of gem-dimethyl groups and the carboxyl-group-mediated interactions, the formation of nanoscale closed pores was facilitated while the continuity of sp2-hybridized carbon microcrystals was ensured and a large interlayer spacing was maintained. Through this approach, an HC architecture with elongated pseudo-graphitic domains and abundant closed pores is constructed in a synergistic manner, affording excellent electronic and ionic transport kinetics. The engineered HC exhibits an enhanced reversible capacity of 427.5 mAh g–1 and an outstanding initial coulombic efficiency (ICE) of 90.18%, along with a high reversible initial capacity of 346.7 mAh g–1 at 2 A g–1 and a capacity retention of up to 85.3% after 500 cycles. This study provides new insights into the microstructural design for high-capacity, high-rate sodium storage.

title: Design and Synthesis of Nonfused Medium-Wide-Bandgap Acceptors for High-Efficiency Organic Photovoltaic Cells
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract With the continuous exploration of organic photovoltaic (OPV) applications, medium-wide bandgap (MWBG) OPV cells demonstrate substantial potential for emerging applications, particularly in indoor environments. However, most high-performance MWBG acceptors rely on costly fused conjugated backbones, limiting the industrialization of MWBG OPV cells. Here, we report a nonfused MWBG acceptor, TBT-59, designed from a thiophene–benzene–thiophene central unit with bulky 2,4,6-trimethylphenyl side chains to modulate its molecular conformation. Due to a simple synthetic route, TBT-59 displays a low material cost of 12.50$·g–1. When blended with PB2, TBT-59 exhibits higher electron mobility, more balanced charge transport, and lower voltage loss than TBT-65. Therefore, the TBT-59-based OPV cell achieves a power conversion efficiency of 13.9%, among the best for nonfused MWBG acceptors with absorption onsets below 800 nm. Under 2700 K light-emitting diode illumination at 1000 lux, the TBT-59-based cell reaches an efficiency of 24.1%. This work demonstrates a cost-effective design strategy for MWBG acceptors.

title: Hierarchically Structured All-Polymer Composites for Enhanced High-Temperature Energy Storage
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Polymer dielectrics are promising candidates for high-temperature capacitive energy storage owing to the intrinsic electrical insulation and processing advantages. However, conventional polymer dielectrics usually suffer from low energy density and efficiency at elevated temperatures due to the difficulty in simultaneously achieving a strong polarization response and a high breakdown strength. Here, we propose a trilayer coaxial nanofiber hierarchical architecture to improve high-temperature energy storage performance. By confining highly polar polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF) to the middle layer and utilizing thermally stable polyetherimide (PEI) to form inner and outer insulating barriers, such hierarchical interface design enhances dielectric displacement while suppressing leakage conduction loss at high temperatures. Based on the optimized PVDF/PEI film, boron nitride (BN) nanowhiskers are incorporated into the PVDF layer to further improve voltage resistance and performance stability under elevated-temperature conditions. Benefiting from the synergistic regulation of polarization response, charge blocking, and breakdown reliability, the 1 wt % BN-15% PVDF/PEI nanocomposite film delivers a high energy density of 10.52 J cm–3 with 96% discharge efficiency at 150 °C under a maximum applied electric field of 750 kV mm–1. This work establishes a scalable and low-cost design strategy for improving the high-temperature performance of polymer-based nanocomposite dielectrics through hierarchical structure engineering.

title: Inorganic Ionic Polymerization toward Fracture-Resistant, Self-healable Functional Hydrogels
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Fracture-resistant, self-healable functional hydrogels hold promise for soft robotics, wearable electronics, and intelligent devices. However, integrating these properties within a single structure remains challenging. Persistent load-bearing constraints hinder molecular rearrangement for repair, whereas excessive network dynamics can disrupt functional organization. Here, we uncover a reciprocal assembly mechanism based on bidirectional regulation between inorganic ionic oligomers and polymer chains. The acrylic acid/poly(acrylic acid) (PAA) environment suppresses calcium carbonate oligomer (CCO) aggregation, while CCO organizes PAA chains into birefringent acicular domains through multisite coordination and cooperative hydrogen bonding. These domains provide persistent load-bearing constraints and exchangeable interactions, enabling a fracture energy of 38.3 kJ m–2 and 87% tensile-strength recovery after 6 h of ambient healing. The same assembled network further exhibits 4.5% AM1.5G solar-weighted absorptivity and strong mid-infrared emission, remaining 5.1 °C cooler than neat PAA under simulated sunlight while retaining its cooling response for 21 days. This work establishes inorganic ionic oligomers as active reciprocal regulators of polymer organization, coupling dynamic network reconstruction with mechanical reinforcement and functional stability.

title: Chromophore Orientation as a Design Strategy for Self-Assembled Monolayers in p-i-n Perovskite Solar Cells
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Self-assembled monolayers of the carbazole-based phosphonic acids recently became a popular choice for hole-selective layers in p-i-n perovskite solar cells. However, the role of molecular geometry in controlling interfacial coverage and device performance remains poorly understood. In this work, we have investigated anchor-to-chromophore connectivity as a molecular design parameter by synthesizing four carbazole phosphonic acid derivatives with T-shape and Rod-shape structures. The molecular pairs were designed to keep similar energetic properties while varying the spatial orientation of the chromophore relative to the phosphonic acid anchoring group. Optical spectroscopy and photoemission yield measurements confirm that the energy levels are governed primarily by the substitution position on the carbazole core, rather than by molecular orientation. In contrast, electrochemical impedance and cyclic voltammetry measurements reveal pronounced differences in charge-transfer blocking ability, indicating improved ITO surface coverage for Rod-shape molecules. When implemented in p-i-n perovskite solar cells, Rod-shape interlayers provide a reproducible improvement in device performance, although in part hindered by less favorable wetting behavior. After mitigating film formation and top interface losses, devices with 3-Rod reached a power conversion efficiency of 25.04%. These results demonstrate the importance of chromophore orientation for designing densely packed, high-performance phosphonic acid materials for perovskite solar cells.

title: Electron-Rich Cobalt Single-Atom Sites via Axial GaN Coordination Boost CO2-to-CO Conversion through an Optimized *COOH Pathway
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Precise tuning of the electronic structure of single-atom metal sites at their atomic scale to surpass their intrinsic activity and selectivity limits remains a fundamental challenge. Here, we constructed a well-defined electron-rich single-atom Co site by loading cobalt phthalocyanine (CoPc) molecules with CoN4 centers onto the gallium nitride (GaN) substrate (CoPc@GaN). Characterization analysis reveals that the work function difference between the GaN substrate and CoPc induces an interfacial built-in electric field (BEF), which drives electron transfer from GaN to the CoN4 center, forming electron-rich Co active sites. This configuration effectively optimizes the adsorption/dsorption behavior of reaction intermediates (*COOH and *CO) during CO2RR. In the H-type cell, CoPc@GaN achieves a CO Faradaic efficiency of 97.9% at –0.9 V (vs RHE), while in a flow cell, the efficiency increases to 98.8% at –1.0 V (vs RHE). The electrocatalyst maintains >90% selectivity across a broad potential window of 1000 mV and demonstrates stable performance over 32 h. In situ attenuated total reflection Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (ATR-FTIR) and density functional theory (DFT) calculations further reveal that the electron-rich Co active sites significantly reduce the energy barrier for *COOH formation and facilitate CO desorption, validating the feasibility of the strategy of modulating metal phthalocyanines through substrate engineering.

title: Naphthalene-Fused Meta-Dual-Boron Compounds Enable an 80 nm Red Shift with Concurrently Narrowed Full Widths at Half Maximum
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Multiple resonance emitters are highly sought after for their intrinsically narrowband emission, yet achieving long-wavelength emission without spectral broadening remains a critical challenge. Herein, we report a naphthalene-fused rigid π-extension strategy based on the meta-positioned dual boron framework BBCz-DB by replacing its peripheral carbazole units with naphthalene fragments to develop the yellow MR emitter DB-CzNa. This molecular design leverages the dual aromaticity of naphthalene: while the global π-delocalization effectively narrows the energy gap, the preserved local aromaticity maintains a highly rigid molecular framework, which significantly suppresses excited-state vibronic coupling. This synergistic effect allows the MR emitters to achieve a pronounced emission red shift without sacrificing their narrow emission characteristics. Consequently, DB-CzNa achieves an 80 nm red shift relative to BBCz-DB, delivering yellow emission at 546 nm with an ultra-narrow full width at half maximum of 16 nm (0.07 eV) in toluene. A sensitized fluorescence organic light emitting diode device based on DB-CzNa affords a yellow electroluminescence at 556 nm with a full widths at half maximum of 24 nm and a maximum external quantum efficiency of 26.9%. This work demonstrates that judicious naphthalene fusion on meta-dual boron frameworks provides a powerful strategy to overcome the trade-off between spectral redshift and broadening.

title: Solar-Matched Colloidal Quantum Dots/Metal–Organic Framework Hybrid Materials for Photo-Induced Charge Transfer
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Lead sulfide colloidal quantum dots (PbS CQDs) are promising third-generation photovoltaic materials, and metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) are complementary materials that are used as multifunctional charge storage and redox platforms. Hybrid materials combining CQDs and MOFs are highly promising for applications utilizing solar-driven charge transfer, but their synthesis can be challenging due to the thermal instability of solar-matched infrared CQDs. Here, we demonstrate a room-temperature, "bottle-around-ship" synthesis of a nanocomposite that integrates near-infrared (NIR) absorbing PbS CQDs with an iron-based MOF, MIL-88B(Fe). We employ a syringe-pump-assisted addition of precursors to achieve controlled nucleation and crystallization of the MOF around the CQDs under ambient conditions. Structural characterization confirms the formation of crystalline composites composed of co-localized CQDs with the MOFs. Steady-state, time-resolved optical spectroscopy reveals photoluminescence quenching and shortening of the exciton lifetime in the composite compared to the CQDs alone. Transient absorption data suggest a photo-induced charge transfer from the PbS CQDs to the MIL-88B(Fe) framework on a picosecond timescale. This work establishes a room-temperature synthesis approach for integrating thermally sensitive solar-matched CQDs with functional MOFs and performs an initial spectroscopic study to evaluate the potential of these nanocomposites as advanced hybrid materials for photocatalysis and optoelectrochemical devices in the future.

title: Thiophene-Ring Triggered Channel Curving Enables the Separation of Benzene and Cyclohexane via Sieving
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The separation of benzene and cyclohexane remains a formidable challenge in the petrochemical industry. Herein, we propose a strategy to synergistically modulate the geometric and electronic properties of MOF frameworks. A novel 2D layered MOF (SYUCT-112) was constructed using 1,3-bis((2-methylimidazol-1-yl)methyl)benzene (1,3-bmimb) as the primary ligand and 2,5-thiophenedicarboxylic acid (H2TDC) as the auxiliary ligand. Benefiting from the intrinsic curved configuration and electron-rich nature of H2TDC, the thiophene-ring triggers a structural transformation from a 3D interpenetrated framework to a 2D layered architecture via a structural corner effect. More importantly, well-defined curved pore channels of 5.2 Å are fabricated, enabling precise size-sieving separation of benzene and cyclohexane. Adsorption measurements show that SYUCT-112 possesses a high benzene uptake of 105.9 mg g–1 and delivers an adsorption selectivity factor of 27.78 toward benzene/cyclohexane, accompanied by excellent recyclability. Molecular simulations further confirm that the superior benzene selectivity stems from the size-sieving effect of the curved channels and abundant weak inter-molecular interactions, including S···π and C–H···S contacts. This work provides an instructive guideline for the rational design of porous materials toward targeted molecular sieving applications.

title: Confronting water bankruptcy
source: Nature Sustainability
abstract: With 2030 and the conclusion of the current round of Sustainable Development Goals on the horizon, the world has entered a state of water bankruptcy. A collection of opinion and research explores how this bankruptcy affects environmental and social systems and asks how we return to sustainable and resilient water futures.

title: A Sandwich-Structured Dual-Mode Fabric with Temperature-Adaptive Spectral Tunability for All-Season Outdoor Personal Thermal Management
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Owing to global warming, sudden temperature fluctuations are occurring with greater frequency, which exacerbates risks to public health. Passive radiative cooling and solar heating technologies have unique advantages of requiring no energy input, rendering them highly suitable for thermal management textiles. The operation of the dual-mode fabric with cooling and heating functions primarily relies on the contrast between the solar reflectance on the cooling side and solar absorption on the heating side. However, the regulation of infrared emissivity in both modes tends to be ignored. Here, we report a dual-mode woven fabric based on a sandwich structure that features temperature-adaptive spectral tunability for all-season outdoor personal thermal management. The combination of a polydimethylsiloxane/nano-zinc oxide (PDMS/nano-ZnO) radiative cooling layer with a polydopamine (PDA) solar heating layer constituted the basis of the dual-mode switchable fabric. More importantly, the introduction of eicosane into the porous fibers realized the spectral tunability in response to ambient temperature. The solar reflectance in the cooling mode showed an increase of nearly 6% at high temperature (>40 °C), while the infrared emissivity in the heating mode was reduced by 13.4% at low temperature (<10 °C). In addition, the introduction of eicosane also endowed the fabric with considerable latent heat to further improve thermal management performance. Its temperature range of response corresponds closely to the human thermal comfort zone. Under solar intensity (Isolar) of ∼500 W/m2, the resulting fabric achieved a temperature increase of ∼7.1 °C compared with bare skin in the heating mode and maintained the average temperature of the covered skin close to that of bare skin in the cooling mode. Thanks to the woven structure, the fabric exhibited desirable mechanical strength, waterproofness, washability, breathability, and moisture permeability. This dual-mode woven fabric was expected to provide further insight into developing responsive dual-mode personal thermal management textiles.

title: Particle Size Engineering of Injectable Poly( l -lactic Acid) Microspheres Modulates Material−Tissue Interactions and Extracellular Matrix Remodeling
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Injectable poly(l-lactic acid) (PLLA) microspheres have been widely explored as regenerative biomaterials due to their favorable biocompatibility and ability to support extracellular matrix (ECM) formation. However, how microsphere size, as a fundamental structural parameter, influences degradation behavior, material−tissue interactions, and subsequent tissue remodeling remains poorly understood. In this study, we developed size-controlled PLLA microsphere systems, including single-sized and multiscale formulations, with polycaprolactone (PCL) microspheres as material controls, to investigate particle size-dependent biological responses. Microsphere size influenced degradation characteristics and was associated with distinct cellular and tissue responses. In vitro studies demonstrated that extracts from 50 μm PLLA microspheres induced stronger fibroblast ECM-related responses among single-sized formulations, accompanied by enhanced expression of LTBP1, COL1A1, COL3A1, and collagen-associated proteins. In vivo, multiscale PLLA microspheres exhibited distinct macrophage response profiles and were associated with more pronounced long-term collagen organization and ECM remodeling. Transcriptomic analysis identified gene-expression patterns associated with extracellular matrix organization, immune regulation, and tissue remodeling. Collectively, these findings identify microsphere size as an important biomaterial design parameter for tuning degradation behavior, host−material interactions, and ECM remodeling, providing a particle size engineering strategy for the development of injectable regenerative biomaterials.

title: Polymer Brushes on Polymerized and Patterned Lipid Bilayers via UV-Initiated RAFT Polymerization
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Patterned lipid membranes functionalized with polymer brushes offer a versatile platform for controlling cell–surface interactions and developing biomimetic cell-culture systems. Here, we report a UV-initiated reversible addition–fragmentation chain-transfer (RAFT) polymerization strategy for synthesizing poly(di(ethylene glycol) methyl ether methacrylate) (PDEGMA) and poly(oligo(ethylene glycol) methyl ether methacrylate) (POEGMA) brushes on polymerized and micropatterned supported lipid bilayers. Atomic force microscopy revealed linear brush growth over time, with POEGMA exhibiting a higher growth rate than PDEGMA. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy confirmed the successful formation of polymer layers on the lipid membranes. Cell-adhesion experiments using NIH 3T3 fibroblasts demonstrated distinct effects of the two brush chemistries: PDEGMA-modified membranes did not significantly reduce cell attachment compared with tissue culture polystyrene, whereas POEGMA-modified membranes exhibited pronounced antifouling properties, significantly reducing cell attachment independently of brush thickness within the investigated range. To provide a route toward surfaces that combine antifouling properties with controlled cell adhesion, POEGMA brushes were extended with a poly(glycidyl methacrylate) (PGMA) block. The successful formation of the block copolymer was confirmed by atomic force microscopy and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The resulting epoxide-functionalized brush architecture provides a basis for future post-polymerization modification with cell-adhesive ligands. This approach combines spatially patterned lipid membranes with chemically tunable polymer brushes, offering opportunities to engineer cell-interactive interfaces for biomimetic cell culture and studies of cell–surface interactions.

title: Liquid Metal–Spent Coffee Ground Composites for Flexible UV-Responsive Electrochemical Sensors
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Sustainable functional materials derived from biomass waste offer promising opportunities for flexible electronics and photoresponsive systems. Herein, we report liquid metal gallium–spent coffee grounds–ethyl cellulose (Ga–SCGs–EC) composite films fabricated through particle-size reduction of SCGs, sonication-assisted Ga dispersion, and solution casting with EC as a binder matrix. The incorporation of Ga droplets, with their self-limiting 2D Ga2O3 skins, strongly influenced the film microstructure, leading to increasingly fine and Ga-rich domains as the Ga:SCGs ratio increased from 1:1 to 4:1. Structural and thermal analyses showed that the Ga droplets were physically integrated within the SCGs–EC matrix and predominantly retained liquid-state characteristics. Mechanical testing showed that Ga addition improved tensile performance, with the 1:1 composition exhibiting the highest mechanical reinforcement. In contrast, the 4:1 film displayed the strongest photoresponsive behavior, showing reversible and wavelength-dependent current modulation, particularly under 385 nm UV illumination. This enhanced response was associated with improved Ga dispersion and light-induced interfacial charge modulation involving native Ga/Ga2O3 interfaces and oxygen deficiency in Ga2O3. These findings highlight Ga–SCGs–EC films as flexible, biomass-derived composites with photoresponsive properties that can be readily integrated as electrodes for UV detection.

title: Dual-Targeted Thalidomide Nanoliposomes Suppress Neutrophil-Driven Inflammation in Intestinal Behçet’s Disease
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Excessive neutrophil recruitment, vascular activation, and platelet-associated inflammatory interfaces are implicated in intestinal tissue injury in intestinal Behçet’s disease (intestinal BD), whereas conventional systemic therapies offer limited spatial control over drug exposure within active intestinal lesions. Here, we developed thalidomide-loaded nanoliposomes co-functionalized with a neutrophil elastase-binding peptide (NEBP) and a P-selectin-binding peptide (PSN), designated Thd-NEBP/PSN-Lip, to engage complementary activated neutrophil-associated and P-selectin-associated inflammatory interfaces. Thd-NEBP/PSN-Lip exhibited a mean hydrodynamic diameter of 116.6 ± 5.7 nm, a thalidomide encapsulation efficiency of 91.43 ± 0.71%, and reduced initial burst release, while maintaining colloidal stability during storage and simulated gastrointestinal exposure. Surface ligand density was estimated from the feed composition. Ligand-dependent interactions were observed in activated endothelial cells and neutrophil-like cells; in activated endothelial cells, liposome-associated fluorescence increased from 7.42% for Thd-Lip to 40.55% for Thd-NEBP/PSN-Lip and decreased to 1.10% following free PSN competition. Additional validation supported PSN-dependent association with activated platelets and greater inflamed-tissue association of the dual-ligand formulation than with either single-ligand formulation. In vivo, Thd-NEBP/PSN-Lip showed preferential and prolonged retention within inflamed intestinal tissues, with intestinal fluorescence remaining approximately 2.6-fold higher than that of Thd-Lip at 24 h. LC–MS/MS quantification further showed increased total intestinal thalidomide exposure and a higher intestine/plasma concentration ratio after Thd-NEBP/PSN-Lip administration. In a murine intestinal BD-like model, Thd-NEBP/PSN-Lip alleviated intestinal injury, restored colon length toward the healthy level, reduced neutrophil infiltration and local inflammatory cytokine expression, attenuated responses involving IL-17A+CD4+ and IFN-γ+CD4+ T cells, and partially restored the Foxp3+ regulatory T cell compartment. Microbiome, metabolomic, and transcriptomic analyses further indicated broader treatment-associated changes in the intestinal inflammatory microenvironment. Collectively, these findings suggest that dual-targeted nanoliposomes improve lesion-directed thalidomide delivery and suppress neutrophil-driven intestinal inflammation, supporting a pathology-guided nanotherapeutic strategy for intestinal BD.

title: Mpox virus replication and drug resistance in the central nervous system of a man with advanced human immunodeficiency virus at autopsy
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Mpox virus (MPXV) clade IIb caused an outbreak of >100,000 cases globally, with highest disease burden in people living with advanced human immunodeficiency virus (HIV), those with CD4 count 3. We performed an extensive autopsy on a fatal case of mpox in a man living with advanced HIV-1, who achieved HIV suppression but poor immune reconstitution despite > 6 months antiretroviral therapy and had progressive necrotizing mucocutaneous mpox disease despite multiple prolonged mpox-targeted therapies. We quantified MPXV DNA across 76 autopsy samples from different anatomical sites and observed a high burden in skin and mucosal tissue and a lower burden in all central nervous system (CNS) tissues tested. However, we detected replication-competent MPXV in multiple CNS tissues and confirmed neuronal and glial cell infection using RNA-scope in situ hybridization. MPXV sequencing from body and brain tissues revealed widespread tecovirimat resistance-associated variants. This case proves that replication-competent MPXV and tecovirimat resistance-associated isolates can infect and persist in the CNS of people with advanced HIV thus informing future therapeutic design.

title: Ligand-Mediated Long-Range Interactions Enable Selective Activation of H2O2 for Efficient Water Decontamination
source: Earth and environmental sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Steering hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) activation to selectively generate superoxide radicals (O2•−) offers a potent solution for water decontamination, especially under neutral or even alkaline conditions. However, the practical potential of this approach has long been constrained by inefficient O2•− generation due to non-selective O–H bond cleavage during H2O2 activation. Here, we develop a biomimetic second coordination sphere engineering (BSCSE) strategy to synthesize a meso-tetra(4-carboxyphenyl)porphyrin iron (TCPP-Fe) catalyst that directs heterolytic O–H bond cleavage during H2O2 activation, leading to predominant O2•− generation with an apparent O2•− generative selectivity of 90.3% among the quantified reactive oxygen species. The TCPP-Fe catalyst exhibits exceptional catalytic performance, achieving a normalized apparent rate constant of 40.6L2min−1gH2O2−1gcat.−1" role="presentation">40.6L2min−1gH2O2−1gcat.−140.6\,{{{{\rm{L}}}}}^{2}\,{\min }^{-1}\,{{{{{\rm{g}}}}}_{{{{{\rm{H}}}}}_{2}{{{{\rm{O}}}}}_{2}}}^{-1}\,{{{{{\rm{g}}}}}_{{{{\rm{cat}}}}.}}^{-1}, which is approximately 2.1-fold higher than the next-highest value in the compiled dataset of representative Fe-based, Fe-alloy, and related catalysts. This remarkable reactivity and selectivity arise from BSCSE-induced modulation of the electronic structure of Fe sites, which facilitates efficient electron transfer between H2O2 and Fe centers while electrostatically stabilizing the Fe–*OOH intermediate to steer O2•− generation. Integrated into a continuous-flow catalytic membrane filtration system treating real secondary effluent, TCPP-Fe enables >96% bisphenol A removal with negligible Fe leaching and sustained removal performance during 120 h of operation. This work bridges biomimetic principles with heterogeneous catalysis, providing a generalizable design strategy for next-generation catalysts toward sustainable water decontamination.

title: Mapping redox networks in cardiomyocytes reveals non-overlapping response pathways for cytosolic versus mitochondrial H₂O₂ signaling
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Reactive oxygen species (ROS) are essential redox messengers, yet their effects depend on concentration, localization, and duration. Here, we investigate how compartment-specific hydrogen peroxide (H₂O₂) production influences cardiomyocyte redox signaling and function. Using human induced pluripotent stem cell–derived cardiomyocytes (iPSC-CM) expressing the H₂O₂ biosensor HyPer fused to D-amino acid oxidase (DAO), we achieve chemogenetic control of H₂O₂ generation in the cytosol, mitochondria, or nucleus. Cytosolic H₂O₂ propagates throughout the cell, whereas mitochondrially generated H₂O₂ remains spatially restricted, reflecting compartmentalized antioxidant buffering. Cytosolic H₂O₂ impairs contractility and relaxation in both 2D and 3D engineered heart tissue models, accompanied by preferential oxidation of Z-disc–associated and actin-binding proteins and by altered sarcomere organization. Antioxidant treatment attenuates these effects. In contrast, mitochondrially produced H₂O₂ is better tolerated and associated with adaptive redox remodeling, with preserved contractile performance that is antagonized by conoidin A-induced inhibition of cytosolic peroxiredoxin activity. These findings demonstrate that the subcellular source of H₂O₂ shapes redox propagation, oxidation patterns, and functional responses, highlighting redox compartmentalization as a determinant of cardiomyocyte performance and stress resilience.

title: Hydroxyl-mediated oxygen anchoring steers CO electroreduction toward ethanol
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Electrochemical conversion of carbon monoxide (CO) to ethanol is challenged by competing pathways that remove oxygen from reaction intermediates and form ethylene. Here we show that strontium (Sr)-modified copper (Cu) promotes ethanol formation and propose hydroxyl-mediated oxygen anchoring as a mechanism for oxygen-retention. Sr-derived sites are proposed to host hydroxyl adjacent to Cu reaction sites, creating a site-differentiated interface that shift hydroxyl from site-competing spectators to selectivity-directing components. In situ spectroscopy reveals Sr-dependent changes in signals associated with adsorbed CO and oxygen-containing intermediates. Calculations suggest that nearby Sr–OH groups can stabilize the oxygen-ends of selected intermediates through non-covalent interactions, mitigating C–O bond weakening. The resulting Sr(1.0%)-Cu catalyst achieves an ethanol Faradaic efficiency (FE) of 65.4% at 1.0 A cm−2, with an ethanol-to-ethylene FE ratio of ~18.7, compared with a maximum of ~2.0 for pristine Cu. It also operates for over 200 hours in a membrane-electrode assembly and retains ethanol selectivity under syngas feeds. These findings highlight the spatial organization of interfacial hydroxyl species as a strategy for oxygen-retaining electrosynthesis.

title: Gut microbiota GABA regulation by intestinal pH osmolality and microbial consumption
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The production of gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA) by the gut microbiota has garnered attention due to its potential role as a driver of gut-brain axis signaling. However, mechanisms regulating microbiota-derived GABA under physiological conditions remain unclear. Here, we identified low pH and high osmolality as promoters of GABA production in the gut microbe Bacteroides thetaiotaomicron by driving changes in the expression of the glutamate decarboxylase system. pH also emerged as a critical factor for enhancing GABA production in a broader set of gut microbes. However, in the cecal microbiota of specific pathogen-free mice and in an ex vivo model of the human colon microbiota, GABA levels did not increase under physiologically relevant acidic conditions. This can partly be explained by microbial GABA consumption. Consistently, reducing cecal pH increased GABA levels in Oligo-MM12 mice, a gnotobiotic model lacking GABA-consuming gut microbes. Our findings highlight the intricate balance between gut microbial GABA production, consumption, and environmental factors such as pH and osmolality.

title: In vivo dynamics of ovulation and oocyte entrance into the oviduct in mice
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Ovulation is a dynamic multistep process essential for female fertility. Although central to reproductive success, the real-time behaviors of oocytes, ovarian tissues, and oviducts during the ovulatory process in vivo remain unknown. Here, we use intravital microscale volumetric imaging to reveal the in vivo spatiotemporal dynamics of key stages of ovulation associated with follicle opening, oocyte release, and the subsequent transport of the ovulated oocyte into the oviduct in mice. Unexpectedly, we find a time lag between follicle opening and subsequent abrupt changes in follicular volume and oocyte position, followed by the release of the cumulus-oocyte complex (COC). Remarkably, oocytes deform into an elliptical shape as they squeeze through a relatively small opening of the follicle but regain a spherical shape shortly after being released. We also discover repetitive pulses of fluid emitted from the oviduct that inflate the periovarian space, increasing fluid flow required for COC movement into the oviduct. These findings uncover previously unrecognized cellular, tissue, and organ-level mechanisms that coordinate ovulation and oocyte transport, offering potential insights into the etiology of ovulatory disorders and female infertility.

title: Single-cell mass accumulation reveals copiotrophic bacterial growth rates in native seawater
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The growth of marine microbial communities drives ocean biogeochemical cycles, yet the growth rates of individual species remain poorly understood. Copiotrophic bacteria, such as Vibrio species, are thought to live a feast-and-famine existence, as their capacity for rapid growth contrasts with their typically low abundance. Here we use a microfluidic mass sensor adapted to directly measure subtle and otherwise undetectable mass accumulation of individual marine bacteria in native seawater. We observe growth of several copiotrophic bacteria and find that Vibrio species consistently grew across diverse temporal conditions and had higher buoyant mass than co-occurring species. Remarkably, their growth rates were similar across samples collected over days to months and followed a well-known nutrient growth law previously established in laboratory cultures. Overall, our findings suggest that low-abundance species may play a disproportionately large role in the marine carbon cycle, with rapid biomass turnover driven by high growth rates balanced by intense predation.

title: A map of multi-omics quantitative trait loci in a Chinese population reveals regulatory variations and disease links
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Quantitative trait loci (QTL) studies have been pivotal in mapping the genetic regulation of molecular traits but have been primarily conducted in European populations, limiting insights into diverse ethnic groups. To close this knowledge gap, we conduct a large-scale multi-omics QTL analysis using blood samples from 3,102 Chinese individuals, systematically characterizing the regulatory effects of genetic variants on DNA methylation, plasma levels of 365 inflammation-related proteins, and metabolites. Our study identifies 209 protein QTLs (pQTLs) for 155 proteins and 587 metabolite QTLs (metabQTLs) for 369 metabolites. By integrating these findings with cis-methylation QTL (meQTL) from our previous work, we define the shared genetic architecture across molecular layers. Colocalization analyses reveal 3,665 pairs of shared causal variants across traits, including loci such as LHPP, with mediation evidence supporting regulatory cascades linking DNA methylation, proteins, and metabolites. To link these molecular findings to health outcomes, we perform Mendelian randomization (MR) analyses, identifying 497 potential causal relationships between molecular traits and diseases, including FCRL3 for Graves’ disease and deoxycholic acid 3-glucuronide for colorectal cancer. Collectively, we present a systematic genomic atlas of meQTLs, pQTLs, and metabQTLs specific to East Asian populations, providing critical insight into shared regulatory networks and candidate causal variants across molecular and disease phenotypes.

title: Expansion of North Atlantic Deep Water during Northern Hemisphere Glaciation
source: Earth and environmental sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation (AMOC) is a major driver of the Earth’s climate, moving heat from the Southern Hemisphere to the Northern Hemisphere. Neither foraminiferal carbon isotope records nor modelling studies agree on the spatial extent of North Atlantic Deep Water (NADW), the northern deep limb of the AMOC, over the intensification of Northern Hemisphere Glaciation (iNHG, ~2.73 million years ago). Here we present high-resolution neodymium isotope (εNd) records from a depth transect in the equatorial Atlantic over the iNHG. We find a persistent latitudinal and depth gradient in neodymium isotope values in the deep Atlantic during the Late Pliocene, absent in the Early Pleistocene, indicating an expansion of NADW extent over the iNHG. In contrast, our reconstruction suggests very little glacial-interglacial variability in NADW extent during both the Late Pliocene and Early Pleistocene. These results suggest deep-water circulation was substantially different during a warm climate state, with implications for the role of NADW formation during major climate transitions and its future stability.

title: Sinking land is the fingerprint of global water bankruptcy
source: Nature Sustainability
abstract: Land subsidence is the physical fingerprint of irreversible groundwater loss, yet remains absent from water governance. Embedding it as an early warning metric could help societies act before depletion becomes water bankruptcy.

title: Dearomatization and cycloaddition of furans and indoles enable divergent syntheses of spirooxindole alkaloids
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Dearomatization has revived recently as a key tactic in organic synthesis due to major methodological developments that allow mild chemoselective dearomatization. A major challenge of this dearomatization tactic to strategically couple different dearomatization products and the cycloaddition of two different dearomatization products remains underdeveloped. Herein, we report the development of green oxidative dearomatization of indoles and furans and their formal cycloaddition reaction, leading to efficient construction of versatile biologically active tetracyclic spirooxindoles. Oxidation of furan derivatives (furfuryl amides) induces concomitant rearrangement (aza-Achmatowicz rearrangement) to provide 3-piperidones, which for the first time are elaborated with 3-4 steps to functionalized 1-piperideines and react with 3-(2-bromoethyl)−2-oxindoles derived from green oxidative dearomatization of indoles. This synthetic strategy enables rapid collective synthesis of >30 spirooxindoles within 7 steps and 10 spirooxindole natural products within 10-14 steps with satisfactory overall yields. This work establishes a blueprint for coupling distinct dearomatization manifolds in complex molecule synthesis, with immediate implications for medicinal chemistry and natural product-inspired drug discovery.

title: Educational bankruptcy in a water-insecure world
source: Nature Sustainability
abstract: Engineers can enter the water sector through undergraduate engineering programmes that give limited attention to systems thinking, governance literacy and agency. Where these capabilities remain underdeveloped, the resulting mismatch constitutes an educational bankruptcy that can threaten water security.

title: Exciton binding regulation in oxygen-independent tumor photooxidation enables synchronous photoluminescence for cancer theranostics
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Overcoming the accuracy-efficiency trade-off in light-driven cancer therapy remains a significant challenge for theranostics. Herein, we report a fullerene-loaded heptazine‒perylene (HP/C60) nanopolymer that enables the oxygen-independent oxidation of intracellular biomolecules via photogenerated hole transfer (+1.53 V vs. NHE). Concurrently, HP/C60 facilitates cancer theranostics through spatiotemporal fluorescence imaging with resistance to photobleaching. By precisely tuning the exciton binding energy through controlled interface-induced charge delocalization, we optimize the ratio of exciton recombination and dissociation pathways, enabling the rational allocation of photoluminescence for high-contrast bioimaging and photooxidation for efficient tumor elimination. A 20-minute red light irradiation of HP/C60 is sufficient to initiate the complete ablation of solid tumors of female mice, with the entire therapeutic process monitored via real-time fluorescence imaging. This work establishes exciton management as a universal design principle to synchronize photooxidation and photoluminescence and supports the development of organic semiconductors for cancer theranostics.

title: Stepwise transitions unlock three spin states and diverse SHG in a polar Fe(III) spin-crossover complex
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Multifunctional spin-crossover materials are promising for information storage and nonlinear optics, yet stepwise spin-crossover coupled with controllable second harmonic generation switching is hindered by poor thermal stability of non-centrosymmetric lattices. Herein, we report an air-stable polar Fe(III) spin-crossover complex displaying cooling-induced two-step spin-crossover but one-step transition during heating, delivering a wide thermal hysteresis of 75 K (199 K cooling / 274 K heating) via intense intermolecular cooperativity. Sequential phase evolution (P1 → P1 → Pn) creates three discrete spin configurations with c-axis cell duplication followed by a symmetry-increasing transition to full low-spin phase upon cooling. Second harmonic generation tests verify three separable nonlinear optical states consistent with magnetic responses. Crystal stacking analysis and density functional theory calculations validate that spin ordering-phase transition synergy rearranges molecular dipoles to realize stepwise second harmonic generation modulation. This study offers an original route toward dual spin-optic functional materials for optical storage applications.

title: Upcycling of polyolefin and polyester mixtures via a single-atom alloy
source: Earth and environmental sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Upcycling of mixed plastic waste is challenging due to the complex compositions and high sorting costs, lacking robust catalysts for simultaneous conversion of polyolefins and polyesters. Herein, guided by machine learning, we design a Ru1Cu/CeO2-GR single-atom alloy catalyst that enables one-pot hydrogenolysis of mixed plastics into fuel-range hydrocarbons. Ru single atoms anchored on Cu nanoparticles lower C–C bond cleavage barriers, while Cu suppresses benzene ring overhydrogenation. Under mild conditions (280 °C, 30 bar H2), the catalyst delivers ~75% liquid yield (C5–C22) with 59.5%–62.7% C8–C16 fraction and ~15% aromatic products yield from five-component mixed plastics. Life cycle and techno-economic analyses confirm that this direct upcycling route outperforms traditional sorted recycling with lower environmental impacts and higher economic benefits. This work provides a sustainable and economically viable strategy for mixed plastic waste valorization.

title: Global partnerships for saltwater intrusion
source: Nature Sustainability
abstract: Saltwater intrusion is a global issue with local societal and environmental impacts. Global funding mechanisms will be key in finding place-based solutions.

title: Transforming spinel LiMn2O4 into a Na-layered cathode
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The positive electrode structures of practical sodium-ion batteries are generally confined to polyanionic or layered transition metal oxide frameworks, where the trade-off between specific energy and structural stability limits their application. As a well-established positive electrode structure in lithium-ion batteries, the spinel framework has abundant storage sites for alkali metal ions, but it has received less attention for sodium-ion batteries. Here we show that spinel LiMn2O4 can be transformed into a sodium-ion positive electrode. Electrochemical sodiation drives Mn-ion migration along an octahedral–tetrahedral–octahedral pathway, creating a layered/spinel heterostructure for further sodium storage. Moreover, residual spinel domains inhibit the strain and structural degradation within the layered structure. Consequently, a 26650 cylindrical cell using a LiMn2O4-derived sodium-ion positive electrode achieves a capacity of 3.85 Ah and retains 95.7% capacity after 900 cycles (1.925 A). This work demonstrates that spinel LiMn2O4 can serve as a viable positive electrode for sodium-ion batteries, and that electrochemical transformation is a feasible approach for creating positive electrode frameworks.

title: Constructing radiative dipolar excitons via frontier-state hybridization in 2D perovskites
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Realizing dipolar excitons that simultaneously exhibit strong optical activity and long-range repulsive interactions remains a central challenge in exciton-based nonlinear optics. This challenge stems from the intrinsic trade-off between achieving spatial charge separation, which is necessary for dipole formation, and maintaining sufficient wavefunction overlap to ensure efficient radiative recombination. Here, we overcome this trade-off in the two-dimensional perovskite (AE3T)PbI4 by leveraging organic-inorganic band-edge engineering to induce frontier-state hybridization, thereby forming bright hybridized dipolar excitons with spatially indirect character and appreciable optical transition strength. These excitons combine an out-of-plane permanent electric-dipole component, room-temperature nonlinear transport consistent with long-range dipole–dipole repulsion, and finite optical transition dipole moments. Beyond addressing a key constraint in dipolar-exciton design, this work establishes frontier-state hybridization as a molecular design principle for constructing optically active, electrically polarized excitons in low-dimensional quantum materials.

title: Atomic-level coordination-engineered quantum dots orchestrate mitochondrial energy rescue for diabetic bone regeneration
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Diabetic bone regeneration is critically impaired by a cellular energy crisis that disrupts osteoimmunological processes. While mitochondrial transfer represents a potential metabolic rescue mechanism, this process can be hijacked in diabetes mellitus to propagate inflammation. Current mitochondria-protecting strategies fail to address the spatiotemporal dynamics of intercellular mitochondrial transfer in regenerative tissues. Here, we identify key mitochondrial donor cells, a therapeutically targetable cell population functionally coupled to osteoimmunological outcomes via mitochondrial transfer. We design a nanotherapeutic based on atomic-level coordination-engineered quantum dots to restore functional mitochondrial transfer for energy homeostasis. These quantum dots markedly reduce the ROS catalytic reaction energy barrier and protect mitochondria. Furthermore, their Mn-coordinated degradation fragments activate the CaMKKβ-AMPK signaling axis in diabetes mellitus. This enhanced mitochondrial quality control and transfer efficiency render macrophages competent mitochondria donors. Consequently, our work provides a transformative approach to correct pathological mitochondrial transfer and rescue diabetic bone repair.

title: Full-circle polychromatic photoluminescence in Mn-doped zero-dimensional metal halide under high-pressure
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Polychromatic luminescent materials have attracted sustained interest owing to the potential applications in high-sensitivity visual optical sensing. Nevertheless, developing a rational design strategy that can simultaneously achieve a broad color gamut and tunable multicolor emission remains a highly challenging task. Here we show that a Mn2+-doped zero-dimensional metal halide, Mn2+:(TPA)2PbBr4 (TPA+ = tetrapropylammonium cation), demonstrates these desirable characteristics. By application of high pressure, the initial blue emission of Mn2+:(TPA)2PbBr4 undergoes a sequential transition from cyan to yellow, then to pink-purple, and ultimately returns to blue. This polychromatic color modulation originates from the interplay between the intrinsic blue emission of the [PbBr4]2- tetrahedra and the pressure-induced green-to-red shift of the [MnBr4]2- tetrahedra, accompanied by energy transfer processes between the two luminescent centers. Concurrently, enhanced hydrogen-bonding interactions between the inorganic and organic components suppress nonradiative recombination, increasing the polychromatic emission intensity, which is further amplified at low temperatures. These findings offer new insights into the mechanisms governing polychromatic emission and provide promising strategies for developing advanced optoelectronic materials.

title: Nuclear quadrupole resonance spectroscopy as an operando tool for mechanochemistry
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Mechanochemistry is an expanding and generally green synthetic route, which is attracting more and more chemists in academia and industry. Yet, its applicability is often still limited by the lack of information on the mechanochemical processes. Therefore, to help elucidating reaction pathways in the solid state, we need to develop new real time monitoring techniques. Here we present an operando study of mechanochemical syntheses relying on Nuclear Quadrupole Resonance spectroscopy (NQR). Two mechanochemical syntheses were followed in operando (i.e., real-time in situ) mode by NQR, namely the formation of a halogen-bonded cocrystal and the preparation of a hybrid perovskite, demonstrating potential applications of this original technique, as well as its complementarity to more conventional operando methods used in ball-milling (BM). Lastly, we show that our NQR set-up can also be used in real-time to follow the temperature evolution, during a reaction, directly inside the milling jar. This method, BM-NQR, represents a promising functional alternative to NMR spectroscopy for the real-time monitoring of ball-milling syntheses.

title: Deep strong light-matter coupling in 3D Kane fermions without Dicke criticality
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Deep-strong light-matter coupling is a non-perturbative regime of quantum electrodynamics in which the interaction strength exceeds the frequencies of uncoupled light and matter excitations. Whether a Dicke superradiant phase transition can occur in electronic systems with linear energy-momentum dispersion remains controversial because of the apparent absence of a diamagnetic A2 term in their low-energy Hamiltonian. Here, we investigate Landau polaritons in a bulk mercury cadmium telluride film hosting Kane fermions coupled to a Fabry-Perot resonator. The ultralow cyclotron mass of Kane fermions and a thermally tunable carrier density enable tuning from weak to deep-strong coupling, reaching the single-mode coupling strength of 1.6 above room temperature. Near the Dirac point (100 K), deep-strong coupling coexists with linear low-energy dispersion. Our microscopic quantum theory and classical electromagnetic simulations are in agreement with measured spectra. We conclude that a diamagnetic A2 term emerges despite the linear dispersion, preventing a Dicke superradiant phase transition.

title: Ripple-induced fast-ion losses modeling in the WEST tokamak
source: Nuclear Fusion - latest papers
abstract: The confinement of fast ions is of crucial importance in present and future tokamaks. In typical ion cyclotron resonance heating (ICRH)-heated scenarios in WEST, fast-ion losses can represent more than 20% of the total injected power. To investigate the origin and underlying mechanisms of these losses, we perform simulations of fast hydrogen ion trajectories in a realistic three-dimensional magnetic field. A weighting method is proposed as a post-process to study a particle distribution function with anisotropic temperatures, while preserving uniform statistics in terms of energy. The influence of the initial and final particle position in phase space is studied in details. The simulation results show that ripple losses fall into two categories: deeply trapped particles moving vertically towards the baffle, and drifting bananas striking the antenna along the direction of the magnetic field. If fast particle losses to the baffle can be directly compared with infrared (IR) measurements, diagnosing particles striking the antennas is more challenging, as IR cameras detect a combination of fast-ion losses, plasma heat convection, and radiation. A net reduction of baffle strikes is observed for particles accelerated on the high field side, whereas antenna strikes, in contrast, may be enhanced. Hence, this study suggests that optimizing the ICRH absorption layer position involves a trade-off: reducing deeply trapped losses at the cost of increasing drifting banana losses.

title: Population-level characterisation of the human gut phageome and its association with microbial metabolites
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Bacteriophages, viruses infecting bacteria, are abundant in the human gut, but their population-level structure and metabolic associations remain unclear Here we present a foundational characterisation of the gut phageome using deep shotgun metagenomic data in a large population-based cohort (n = 1,069: TwinsUK). We assembled 116,740 non-redundant vOTUs of which 52.9% were predicted to be temperate and 47.0% virulent. Individuals harboured an average of 3,370 vOTUs, mostly at low abundances, exhibiting structured population-level co-abundance patterns with bacterial species including Faecalibacterium prausnitzii and Blautia wexlerae. Phageome diversity was mostly driven by environmental factors, with modest heritable components. We detected 4 significant vOTU diet associations. Additionally, 6,572 phages were associated with short-chain fatty acids and secondary bile acids, identifying extensive population-level associations between phage-associated genomic variation and microbial metabolites. Over 100 vOTUs encoded auxiliary metabolic genes, while a distinct subset of phages encoded virulence-associated genes, including vacuolating autotransporter toxin (vat) and LPS glucosyltransferases (gtrA, gtrB, gtr) implicated in O-antigen modification and immune invasion, and showed consistent co-abundance patterns with bacterial species previously associated with opportunistic or pathobiont features. These results identify structured population-level associations between phage-associated genomic elements, bacterial communities, and microbial metabolites, motivating future experimental and mechanistic studies.
