title: Dynamic staged solid electrolyte interphase via sequential chemical and electrochemical reactions for highly reversible zinc battery
source: Chem
abstract: Fluorinated cations and anions are incorporated to synergistically restructure the EDL architecture, thereby enabling the formation of a dynamic staged SEI with an organic upper and an inorganic-rich inner via chemical and electrochemical reactions. The preferential adsorption of FPy+ cations promotes adsorption of the OTF− anion at the EDL, thereby engineering an EDL architecture with low active water. This not only facilitates the formation of a dynamic staged SEI film but also effectively mitigates interfacial side reactions.

title: Contemporary synthetic tools for the total synthesis of natural products
source: Chemical Society Reviews advanceAccess
abstract: This Tutorial Review discusses uses of modern synthetic tools in the total synthesis of natural products over the last five years, including photocatalysis, electrochemistry, biocatalysis, skeletal editing, flow chemistry and mechanochemistry.

title: Posterior alpha/beta oscillations reflect oculomotor dynamics underlying subsequent memory effects
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Neural activity and eye movements are well-established predictors of human memory performance. Successful memory formation is associated with reduced alpha/beta power and increased eye movements. However, their coupling and combined contribution to memory formation remain largely unknown. Across four experiments combining eye tracking with scalp or intracranial electroencephalography during free or constrained viewing, we identify the degree of visual exploration, rather than subsequent memory performance, as consistent modulator of posterior alpha/beta power. Going beyond correlations, manipulating eye movements dissociated alpha/beta power reductions from memory. Together with the finding that saccade parameters predicted alpha/beta dynamics, our results directly link posterior alpha/beta activity to the oculomotor system. Moreover, the accumulation of saccades over time accounted for reduced alpha/beta power, resembling the canonical post-stimulus alpha/beta pattern. Our work demonstrates that posterior alpha/beta activity strongly reflects eye movements, supporting alternative perspectives on alpha/beta subsequent memory effects and the general function of posterior alpha/beta activity.

title: Radical addition approaches for 2m/2π-intermolecular reactions of alkenes and alkynes
source: Chemical Society Reviews advanceAccess
abstract: This review organizes radical intermolecular reactions of two π-components through the 2m/2π-synthon framework, highlighting the main strategies used to sort alkene and alkyne partners.

title: Staggered cryo-plasma FIB milling enables high-throughput cryo-ET
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Cryo-focused ion beam (cryo-FIB) milling combined with cryo-electron tomography (cryo-ET) is a crucial technique for studying macromolecules in their native environment. To mill thick samples, plasma ion sources are used. However, the practicality of high plasma currents, which offer the greatest potential for increasing throughput, and their possible damaging effects on the sample have not yet been investigated. Here, we systematically examine high-current xenon plasma-FIB (PFIB) milling and quantify the current-dependent damage in over 4700 tomograms by preparing a total lift-out volume of 9000 µm³. We find that currents of up to 2500 nA can be used in cryo-ET lamella preparations, enabling increased milling speeds and sample volumes that can be examined while maintaining sample integrity. We demonstrate this using a newly developed high-throughput staggered milling routine for waffle-like preparations, in which we achieve high-resolution reconstructions of yeast ribosomes, and for tissue serial lift-outs, enabling a complete experiment within 24 hours. Our results and approach provide a strong foundation for future in situ structural investigations of medically relevant protein complexes in organoids, tissues, or entire organisms.

title: Photobiocatalysis at the interface of biocatalysis and biomimetic chemocatalysis
source: Nature Catalysis
abstract: This Perspective analyses representative photobiocatalytic systems to uncover the synergies between biomimetic and chemomimetic strategies and provides a framework for future developments in the field.

title: Jumping from scaling to scale-up
source: Nature Chemical Engineering
abstract: Jonathan Boreyko discusses how to utilize scaling analysis to progress from fundamental discovery toward practical applications with a close look at capillary-inertial jumping droplets.

title: Partially functional hypomorphic missense variants in BRCA2 are reduced penetrance pathogenic variants
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Identification of partial loss-of-function (hypomorphic), reduced penetrance pathogenic missense variants (RPPVs) and assessment of the clinical relevance of these variants is needed for improved hereditary cancer risk estimation. Here we show that 70 candidate hypomorphic missense variants in the DNA-binding domain of BRCA2 reduce homologous recombination DNA repair activity and endogenous cell survival, decrease RAD51 foci formation, and increase sensitivity to Poly(ADP-ribose) polymerase inhibitors. The 34 “strong” hypomorphs with greatest effects on function are associated with moderate risks of female breast cancer and later ages of diagnosis than pathogenic variants (PVs), and 14 of these variants can be classified as “likely pathogenic” by integration of functional data into a ClinGen BRCA1/2 variant curation model. In addition, 32% of tumors with hypomorphic variants and corresponding loss of heterozygosity for BRCA2 display homologous recombination deficiency (HRD) compared to 83% of tumors with PVs and 7% with benign variants. These RPPVs represent a class of BRCA2 variants that have implications for the clinical management of carriers.

title: Focused ultrasound neuromodulation of mediodorsal thalamus disrupts decision flexibility during reward learning
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: When learning to find the most beneficial course of action, the prefrontal cortex guides decisions by comparing estimates of the relative value of the options available. Basic neuroscience studies in animals support the view that the thalamus can regulate this activity within and across the prefrontal cortex. We studied a group of patients (n = 37) undergoing unilateral MR-guided focused ultrasound for essential tremor, performing the restless bandit, a reward reinforcement learning task, immediately before and after thalamotomy. Thalamotomy significantly impaired the proportion of switch choices during the task without affecting overall performance. This effect was observed when the task was delivered to co-incide with maximal vasogenic thalamic oedema but not in a control group tested on the same day of their treatment. A reinforcement learning model fitted to the patients’ choices replicated the effect of thalamotomy when the model increased exploitation of the bandits’ learnt value estimate. This shift in the explore-exploit trade-off, manifesting as reduced choice flexibility, co-varied with the pattern of post-operative oedema extension into the mediodorsal nucleus. These findings confirm a causal role of the thalamus and specifically the mediodorsal nucleus in regulating the extent to which value estimates are used to guide decisions and learning from reward.

title: STING–IFN–CH25H lipid axis links innate immune activation to tau pathology
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Genetic risk for Alzheimer’s disease and related tauopathies is strongly enriched in pathways governing microglial activation and cholesterol metabolism, yet how these processes converge to drive neurodegeneration remains unclear. Here, we identify the oxysterol 25-hydroxycholesterol (25-HC) as a pathogenic lipid downstream of the cGAS-STING–Interferon (IFN) pathway. In models of tau pathology, interferon signaling induces microglial expression of Cholesterol 25-hydroxylase (CH25H), the enzyme responsible for 25-HC production. Ch25h deletion in female P301S mice suppressed tau aggregation, preserved synapses, prevented brain atrophy, and rescued memory. Mechanistically, loss of CH25H disrupted STING trafficking, attenuated IFN activation, and dampened self-perpetuating microglial inflammation. Strikingly, 25-HC directly accelerated tau propagation in human iPSC-derived neurons. It also disrupted lysosomal and mitochondrial lipid composition, driving cholesteryl ester accumulation and promoting neuronal death under tau-induced stress. These findings define a STING–IFN–CH25H lipid axis that bridges innate immune activation to tau pathology and toxicity, offering a tractable therapeutic pathway for inflammation-driven neurodegenerative conditions.

title: Whole-brain modeling of dynamic causal circuits in human cognition using amortized variational inference
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Understanding dynamic mechanisms underlying cognition remains a major challenge in human neuroscience. Here, we develop, validate, and apply Multivariate Dynamical Systems Identification with Amortized Variational Inference (MDSI-AVI), a computational framework designed to address critical challenges in capturing asymmetric, context-dependent, whole-brain directed interactions while accounting for regional hemodynamic response variability in fMRI data. MDSI-AVI leverages simulation-based inference through forward and reverse variational inference to address the limitations of conventional variational methods in high-dimensional settings. By averaging over uncertainty in hemodynamic response parameters using forward simulation, MDSI-AVI provides well-calibrated posteriors of directed connectivity that scale efficiently to networks with hundreds of nodes. Applied to Human Connectome Project data (N = 728), MDSI-AVI provides insights into working memory mechanisms, identifying the dorsal anterior insula as a critical hub influencing activity at the whole-brain level. We demonstrate task-dependent modulation of causal influences, where the salience network drives frontoparietal network activity, which differentially influences the default mode and sensorimotor networks depending on working memory load. These whole-brain causal interactions distinguish task conditions with high accuracy and predict working memory performance. Our framework demonstrates reproducible results across whole-brain parcellations, establishing MDSI-AVI as a robust tool for advancing our understanding of circuit dynamics in cognition and disease.

title: Lipid droplets amplify inflammasome-driven cytokine secretion in infection and inflammation
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Lipid droplets (LDs) accumulating in infected cells are traditionally viewed as passive nutrient stores exploited by invading pathogens. Here, we show that during infection with virulent Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb), but not BCG, host LDs orchestrate protective immune responses by bridging the ISGylation and inflammasome pathways. Proteomic and imaging analyses reveal the selective recruitment of ISGylated proteins together with caspase-1 and interleukin-1β (IL-1β) precursors to the LD surface. Comparative LD proteomics in wild-type and ISG15-deficient macrophages, combined with ISGylome profiling, identify ISGylated proteins as mediators of pro-IL-1β binding to LDs. Functionally, disruption of LD biogenesis in primary human macrophages impairs mature IL-1β secretion and compromises Mtb control. Notably, this LD-dependent amplification of IL-1β release is not restricted to microbial stimuli but also occurs in response to sterile inflammasome activation. Collectively, these findings redefine LDs as immunoactive organelles integrating microbial and danger signals to potentiate inflammasome-dependent IL-1β responses during infection and inflammation.

title: EpiPack: A computational framework for reference mapping and out-of-reference detection for single-cell ATAC-seq data with heterogeneous peak features
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Despite substantial recent advances in query mapping and cell type or cell state discovery tools, their application to single-cell assay for transposase-accessible chromatin using sequencing (scATAC-seq) data remains challenging. The heterogeneous nature of peak feature spaces across samples hinders the effectiveness of existing methods, while the absence of dedicated tools for detecting perturbed cell types and states in scATAC-seq data further limits the depth of downstream analyses. To address these limitations, we present EpiPack, an integrative computational toolkit that leverages heterogeneous transfer learning and graph-based modeling strategies to advance scATAC-seq analysis. At its core, the Peak Embedding Informed Variational Inference (PEIVI) framework within EpiPack enhances mappable reference construction, query mapping, and label transfer, demonstrating that leveraging heterogeneous features in scATAC-seq data outperforms methods relying solely on conventional homogeneous features. In addition, EpiPack’s global-local out-of-reference (OOR) detection framework achieves robust and efficient detection of perturbed cell types and states, extending the utility of scATAC-seq to disease and perturbation contexts. With its modular design and transferable pre-trained references, EpiPack can be readily applied to diverse analytical tasks and is available as a Python package at https://github.com/ZhangLabGT/EpiPack.

title: Morphogenesis of the muscular ventricular septum is driven by retinoic acid signalling to myocardium
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The mammalian heart is divided into four chambers by septa that isolate systemic and pulmonary circulation and are hotspots of congenital heart defects (CHD). The muscular ventricular septum develops between left and right ventricular cardiomyocytes derived from the first and second heart fields. Despite its clinical importance, mechanisms underlying development of the ventricular septum are poorly understood. Here we show that myocardial reception of retinoic acid (RA) signalling regulates formation of the compact septal core. Activation of a dominant negative RA receptor in second heart field-derived myocardium during septal morphogenesis results in a deep interventricular cleft and bifid cardiac apex. This phenotype is preceded by ectopic trabecular contributions to a RA-independent septal primordium. Molecular analysis identifies defective cardiomyocyte maturation and impaired RAC1 activation in mutant hearts. These results support an infolding and RA-dependent fusion model of septal morphogenesis, providing new insights into ventricular development and the origins of CHD.

title: RSM01, an extended half-life RSV monoclonal antibody with a high barrier to in vitro resistance
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) causes substantial infant morbidity and mortality, particularly in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs). RSM01 is a long-acting RSV monoclonal antibody (mAb) in development for LMICs. In vitro generation of RSM01 resistant mutants has previously been unsuccessful. We systematically assessed the in vitro resistance barrier of RSM01 and the susceptibility of a panel of global contemporary strains to RSM01. Monoclonal antibody resistant mutants (MARMs) were generated by serially passaging triple plaque-purified RSV-A2 and RSV-B1 using HEp-2 cells under pressure from RSM01, nirsevimab, or palivizumab, followed by phenotypic and genotypic characterisation. Moderate resistance was defined as > 3-fold and high resistance as > 30-fold increase in IC50 compared with parental virus. The susceptibility of contemporary global clinical strains to RSM01 was tested in a neutralisation assay. RSV-A and B strains developed high resistance to palivizumab and nirsevimab, while RSM01 pressure induced moderate resistance. No MARMs demonstrated a fitness advantage. RSM01 neutralised global contemporary strains. In conclusion, in vitro RSM01 resistance was infrequent and moderate and RSM01 had broad activity against circulating strains. The confirmation of the high barrier to resistance of RSM01 is encouraging and provides an alternative should resistance emerge with widespread use of current licensed anti-RSV mAbs.

title: Identification of translation events that drive nonsense-mediated mRNA decay reveals functional roles for alternative RNA isoforms
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The nonsense-mediated mRNA decay (NMD) pathway targets mRNAs undergoing premature translation termination for degradation. Previously, RNA-seq of yeast lacking NMD revealed that most genes targeted by NMD lack obvious premature termination codons (PTCs). We develop a combined approach using RNA-seq and 40S ribosome profiling to identify cryptic premature termination events that could account for NMD on nearly all these transcripts, including many alternative RNA transcript isoforms associated with annotated genes. Many NMD-targeted transcripts appear to be involved in two-promoter gene regulatory systems and share properties with long un-decoded transcript isoforms (LUTIs). In particular, we show that the DAL5 LUTI regulates expression of the DAL5 protein-coding mRNA in response to changes to environmental nitrogen. Our work expands the functional roles for LUTIs and establishes the importance of NMD in their regulation.

title: Geopolitical sequencing in Europe's energy transition: infrastructure, legitimacy and finance
source: ScienceDirect Publication: Energy Policy
abstract: Europe's energy transition is increasingly shaped by geopolitical competition, strategic dependence and investment uncertainty. This conceptual paper develops the concept of geopolitical sequencing to explain how geopolitical pressures interact with strategic infrastructure, political legitimacy and transition finance. The central argument is temporal: political commitments, infrastructure development and financing arrangements evolve at different speeds, generating misalignment between strategic ambitions and implementation capacity. Institutional risk compression is introduced as the governance mechanism through which socio-political durability, regulatory credibility and financial arrangements interact to contain or amplify uncertainty. The framework is explored through a case study of Sicily, a strategic Mediterranean energy node connecting North African gas corridors, renewable development, grid interconnections and prospective EU–Africa energy partnerships. Evidence on infrastructure investment, renewable permitting and cross-border financing illustrates how geopolitical priorities interact with territorial distributional tensions, regulatory constraints and investment conditions. The analysis highlights three interconnected challenges: aligning commitments across different time horizons, reconciling system-wide infrastructure benefits with local legitimacy and distinguishing genuine risk reduction from the redistribution of financial exposure. The paper contributes a framework for understanding how geopolitical pressures are transmitted through regional energy transitions and identifies implications for EU energy security, infrastructure governance and transition finance.

title: Vinylcyclopropanes in Rearrangement Reactions
source: Chemical Reviews: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Vinylcyclopropanes constitute highly versatile, strained building blocks whose unique reactivity has enabled the development of a broad variety of synthetically valuable rearrangement and cycloisomerization processes. Over more than six decades of development, vinylcyclopropane chemistry has undergone remarkable evolution, particularly in recent years. Accordingly, these transformations have emerged as powerful tools for the generation of molecular complexity through strain-release-driven reaction manifolds involving both homolytic and heterolytic bond-cleavage mechanistic pathways. This Review provides a comprehensive account of the current state of the art in vinylcyclopropane rearrangement chemistry, with particular emphasis on the mechanistic principles governing these transformations and on their synthetic applications in modern organic synthesis. The different rearrangement modes accessible to vinylcyclopropane derivatives are discussed, including stereomutation processes, vinylcyclopropane-cyclopentene rearrangements, divinylcyclopropane-cycloheptadiene rearrangements, vinylcyclopropane-to-skipped-1,4-diene rearrangements, and cycloisomerization reactions involving specifically functionalized vinylcyclopropane substrates. Particular attention is devoted to the influence of substrate structure, stereochemical features, catalyst design, and thermodynamic and kinetic factors on reaction outcome, in terms of efficiency and selectivity. The broad applicability of these transformations in the synthesis of structurally sophisticated carbo- and heterocyclic architectures, including natural-product-related targets, is highlighted together with current limitations and future opportunities for the continued development of vinylcyclopropane chemistry.

title: Data center cooling in the AI era: cross-scale challenges and system-level outlook
source: ScienceDirect Publication: Applied Energy
abstract: The rapid growth of artificial intelligence (AI) is fundamentally reshaping data center thermal and energy requirements, driven by increasing power densities and heterogeneous workload characteristics. This review provides an integrated cross-scale and temporal perspective that connects AI heat generation with chip-, rack-, and facility-scale thermal management and their interactions with external energy, water, and grid infrastructures. Modern AI workloads, enabled by accelerator-based hardware, can generate highly localized and temporally dynamic heat fluxes, challenging traditional assumptions of uniform and steady-state cooling design. Accordingly, a range of cooling technologies is examined, including air-based systems, liquid cooling approaches, hybrid configurations, and heat-reuse strategies, with emphasis on their performance limits and deployment constraints. The analysis further identifies key cross-cutting barriers to scalability and efficiency, including thermodynamic irreversibility, coupled water–energy–grid dependencies, cross-scale thermal interactions, reliability and maintainability constraints, and technology-specific trade-offs. Building on these observations, future cooling systems are expected to shift toward integrated and adaptive designs that prioritize multi-objective optimization rather than isolated performance improvements. Emerging directions include grid-responsive and water-aware operation, thermal storage-enabled temporal decoupling, co-designed computing and cooling infrastructures, and predictive closed-loop thermal management enabled by digital twins and data-driven control. Collectively, the findings highlight a transition from component-level optimization toward fully integrated system architectures that jointly optimize energy efficiency, resource utilization, operational resilience, and computational performance across spatial and temporal scales.

abstract: Solar desalination offers a sustainable approach to freshwater generation, yet it is fundamentally limited by salt accumulation at evaporation interfaces. While common salt-rejecting strategies can mitigate macroscopic fouling, they fail to achieve real-time monitoring and active management of salts at the metastable stage. Local ion enrichment and associated pre-crystallization processes will degrade efficiency through increased mass-transfer resistance and vaporization enthalpy. title: Van der Waals-modulated integration strategy unlocks scalable fabrication of high-density organic electronic and optoelectronic devices
source: National Science Review Advance Access
abstract: The advancement of organic electronics and optoelectronics fundamentally depends on the development of high-precision integration technologies. However, existing manufacturing approaches for organic semiconductors, particularly conventional photolithography and stencil lithography, are plagued by an intractable trade-off between integration density and device performance. Here we report a van der Waals (vdW)-modulated integration strategy that circumvents this long-standing bottleneck, enabling concurrent high-density and high-performance organic devices. By tailoring the surface chemistry of an ultrathin Parylene shadow mask, we precisely tune interfacial vdW interactions to orchestrate deterministic mask manipulation and high-fidelity patterning. Consequently, organic field-effect transistor (OFET) arrays achieve a device density of 2,500 transistors cm−2 with an average on-state current density of 1.20 μA μm−1, among the highest reported for integrated organic electronics. Furthermore, this strategy is extended to monolithic OFET-organic light-emitting diode (OLED) integration, yielding efficient light-emitting transistor arrays. This work establishes an integration route that preserves the organic semiconductor interface while avoiding direct photolithographic contact with the active layer, opening a route toward large-scale, multifunctional organic integrated systems.

title: Targeted Synthesis of Ni–Pt Diatomic Catalysts by Underpotential Deposition and Galvanic Replacement
source: Advanced Energy Materials
abstract: ABSTRACT Precise construction of heteronuclear dual‐atom sites is essential for improving platinum utilization and oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) performance, yet site‐selective synthesis remains challenging. Herein, we report a targeted electrochemical strategy combining underpotential deposition (UPD) and galvanic replacement (GR) to fabricate atomically dispersed Ni–Pt diatomic sites on sulfur/nitrogen‐codoped carbon (NiPt‐SNC). Sulfur dopants serve as anchoring sites for UPD‐deposited copper, which is replaced by platinum to generate adjacent Ni–Pt pairs. Aberration‐corrected HAADF‐STEM and X‐ray absorption spectroscopy confirm atomic dispersion and reveal Ni–N 3 S and Pt–S 4 coordination. In O 2 ‐saturated 0.1 M KOH, NiPt‐SNC exhibits a half‐wave potential of 0.91 V (vs. RHE), a mass activity of 620 mA mgPt −1 at 0.90 V (8.1‐fold that of Pt/C), with only a 14 mV loss after 10,000 cycles. In zinc‐air batteries, it delivers a peak power density of 320 mW cm −2 and stable operation over 1600 h. Density functional theory reveals that side‐on O 2 adsorption at the Ni–Pt dual site lowers the ORR energy barrier versus single‐site analogues. This work establishes UPD–GR as a targeted route to Ni–Pt diatomic catalysts for durable metal‐air batteries.

title: Vacancy‐Induced Electron Storage Mimicking Natural Photosynthesis for All‐Weather Artificial H 2 O 2 Production
source: Advanced Energy Materials
abstract: ABSTRACT Artificial photosynthesis of H 2 O 2 holds significant potential for solar energy conversion. Nevertheless, its practical application is strictly limited by the intermittent nature of solar irradiation. Here, inspired by the reversible electron storage function of plastoquinone in natural photosynthesis, we design ZnIn 2 S 4 nanosheets with controllable sulfur vacancy concentrations via a sustainable molten salt dynamic confinement strategy, enabling decoupled solar energy utilization. In situ spectroscopic techniques combined with theoretical calculations demonstrate that the vacancies act as electron storage sites that simultaneously promote O 2 adsorption and charge separation. Notably, a reversible photochromic response is detected in the ZnIn 2 S 4 system via photoinduced electron storage, directly visualizing the photo‑charging and dark‑discharging process. Moreover, the charge storage behavior induces a long‐lived carrier‐separated state, which creates a unique stable kinetic platform to drive dark catalytic reactions. After 10 min of photo‑charging, the optimal catalyst (ZIS V ‑M) delivers a “dark” H 2 O 2 yield of 0.21 mmol·g −1 . More importantly, an assembled floating artificial ZIS V ‐M leaf enables sustained and efficient on‐site H 2 O 2 production from open pure water under intermittent natural sunlight and continues H 2 O 2 generation after dark, and the produced H 2 O 2 effectively suppresses the growth of Escherichia coli . This work provides a foundation for developing efficient catalysts for sustainable round‐the‐clock photocatalytic solar energy conversion.

title: Reconciling O 2 Activation with Peroxide Selectivity for H 2 O 2 Photosynthesis Through Orbital Regulation
source: Advanced Energy Materials
abstract: ABSTRACT Artificial photosynthesis of H 2 O 2 from water and air offers a sustainable alternative to the energy‐intensive anthraquinone process. However, efficient H 2 O 2 photosynthesis requires simultaneously activating O 2 while maintaining peroxide selectivity, two requirements that are often difficult to achieve concurrently. Here, we report a bulk‐to‐interface orbital regulation strategy that reconciles O 2 activation with peroxide selectivity in Zn 3 In 2 S 6 . Ru doping tunes the electronic structure of In sites in the bulk, while Ag nanowire anchoring introduces interfacial polarization and light‐driven charge redistribution, collectively strengthening In─O orbital coupling. This continuous orbital regulation promotes O 2 activation while stabilizing the key *OOH intermediate and preserving O─O bond integrity, thereby sustaining selective H 2 O 2 formation. Consequently, the optimized Ru‐Zn 3 In 2 S 6 @Ag nanowires achieve an H 2 O 2 production rate of 63.9 µmol g −1 min −1 in pure water under air without sacrificial agents. Spectroscopic measurements and theoretical calculations reveal that strengthened In─O coupling integrates O 2 activation and *OOH stabilization at electronically regulated In sites. Furthermore, a solar‐driven continuous‐flow reactor sustains outdoor H 2 O 2 production for five consecutive days. These findings identify orbital regulation as a design principle for overcoming activation–selectivity constraints in solar H 2 O 2 photosynthesis.

title: Controlled Film Formation Enables Scalable Wide‐Bandgap Perovskite Modules for Tandem Applications
source: Advanced Energy Materials
abstract: ABSTRACT Wide‐bandgap (WBG) perovskites are essential for high‐efficiency perovskite/silicon tandem solar cells, yet their scalability remains limited by significant efficiency losses upon area upscaling. Here, we establish a scalable blade‐coating strategy for 1.68 eV WBG perovskites by linking coating speed with spatial film formation, optoelectronic uniformity, and device performance. By tuning blade‐coating speed to define a robust process window, we achieve uniform large‐area WBG perovskite films with high reproducibility. The optimized devices deliver a PCE of 20.2% at 0.125 cm 2 and 14.6% at a 100 cm 2 aperture area, corresponding to an active area efficiency loss of only 4.8 percentage points across nearly three orders of magnitude in area. The mini‐modules further exhibit stable operation, maintaining over 85% of initial performance after 800 h (ISOS‐L1) and 89.7% after 300 thermal cycles between ‐40°C to 85°C. The preservation of key photovoltaic parameters suggests that the absorber bandgap remains intact at the module scale. To assess tandem relevance, a 4 cm 2 WBG mini‐module was used as the optical filter on a silicon heterojunction cell in a four‐terminal configuration, yielding a combined power output of 27.8%.

title: Atomic Layer Ordering of 2D van der Waals Ion Channels Enables Ultrathin and Highly Selective Membranes
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Developing ultrathin, highly selective membranes that emulate biological ion channels is a primary goal of synthetic membrane technology. Although two-dimensional (2D) materials offer a promising platform for constructing subnanometer fluidic channels, simultaneously achieving high permeance and excellent selectivity in 2D ionic membranes remains a significant challenge. This bottleneck originates from the complexities involved in controlling the precise structural arrangement within nanosheet assemblies. In this work, we demonstrate that the atomic-layer ordering of 2D van der Waals (vdW) ion channels is a decisive factor in achieving ultrathin, highly selective membranes. By assembling 2D titania nanosheets with atomic layer-by-layer regularity, we fabricate atomic stacking membranes (ASMs) that achieve near-unity ion selectivity within an ultrathin (∼50 nm) framework. The structural regularity of these ASMs causes continuous overlap of the electrical double layer throughout the 2D ion channels, facilitating robust electrostatic regulation and maximizing selectivity. The result is further confirmed by transmission electron microscopy, grazing-incidence wide-angle X-ray scattering analysis, and molecular dynamics simulations. Leveraging the “Lego-like” modular assembly advantage of ASMs, we demonstrate multifunctional heterostructural iontronic devices and gate-controlled iontronic transistors featuring on/off ratios up to 104. Furthermore, the well-ordered 2D ion channels within these ASMs enable high-performance osmotic energy harvesting. This solution-processable atomic-layer van der Waals assembly strategy for ultrathin and highly selective ASMs establishes a versatile platform for uniformly regulating 2D angstrom-scale ion transport, paving the way for advanced biomimetic iontronics and efficient energy conversion.

title: Single-Molecule Fluorescence Imaging Reveals the Kinetic Origin of Wettability-Controlled Photocatalytic Selectivity
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Interfacial wettability strongly influences photocatalytic selectivity, but the kinetic origin of this effect remains unclear. Although adsorption differences and dominant reactive oxygen species (ROS) pathways are often invoked to explain wettability-dependent selectivity, neither fully reveals how interfacial reaction environments determine catalytic outcomes. Here, we use single-molecule fluorescence imaging to directly resolve individual photocatalytic events on reversibly tunable hydrophilic and hydrophobic TiO2 interfaces that preferentially generate •OH- and 1O2-associated reaction environments, respectively. The results show that substrate adsorption remains largely comparable across different wettability states, whereas interfacial conversion kinetics constitute the dominant origin of the observed selectivity and product-release dynamics further amplify this effect. Combined with DFT calculations, the single-molecule analysis reveals the kinetic origin of wettability-controlled photocatalytic selectivity by correlating ROS-associated interfacial environments with interfacial reaction kinetics. This work establishes a single-molecule kinetic analysis framework for interrogating how interfacial microenvironments govern heterogeneous photocatalytic selectivity, providing an approach for linking interfacial regulation to catalytic kinetics and macroscopic outcomes.

title: Self-Induced Spin Glass in Triangular-Lattice MnNCN Stabilized by High-Pressure Synthesis
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The realization of spin glasses in the absence of structural disorder remains an enduring challenge in condensed matter physics and solid-state chemistry. Geometrical frustration provides a route to disordered magnetism in long-range ordered crystals, yet canonical self-induced spin glass (SISG) beyond ultrapure rare-earth elements remains experimentally elusive. Here, we realize a metastable transition-metal SISG phase in MnNCN (R3̅m) via high-pressure and high-temperature (HPHT) synthesis, stabilizing a nonequilibrium state with enhanced magnetic competition. Magnetic measurements establish canonical spin-glass behavior, featuring a freezing temperature of 38.15 K and characteristic slowing-down dynamics, alongside a high coercivity of 1838 Oe. First-principles calculations reveal this SISG behavior is inherently rooted in the frustrated Mn triangular lattice. Mapping the energetic hierarchy uncovers strong competition among distinct antiferromagnetic superexchange pathways. Crucially, high-pressure-driven anisotropic lattice compression alters the Mn-ligand orbital overlap, significantly amplifying the intralayer coupling within the ab triangular planes. This chemical–mechanical modulation intensifies the competition between intralayer and dominant interlayer couplings, producing a strongly frustrated three-dimensional magnetic network. Energy evaluations verify a profound near-degeneracy among these competing states. Rapid quenching kinetically preserves this structurally ordered metastable phase, generating the complex energy landscape characteristic of a spin glass. Electronic-structure analyses further identify the Mn–N–C–N–Mn superexchange pathway mediated by covalent [N═C═N]2– ligands as the origin of magnetic coupling, yielding an intrinsic phase robustness surpassing fragile rare-earth SISGs. Magnetic anisotropy energy (MAE) calculations suggest that the high coercivity mainly arises from extrinsic spin pinning associated with the nanograined microstructure, contributing to macroscopic anti-interference. Ultimately, the creation of the MnNCN SISG and the elucidation of its magnetic competition extend the SISG paradigm to transition-metal compounds, establishing HPHT synthesis as a targeted methodology for tailoring complex magnetism.

title: Tailoring Spin-Crossover Transitions in Fe(HB(tz)3)2 via Cocrystallization for Low-Temperature Barocaloric Cooling
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Spin-crossover (SCO) phase transitions can drive large barocaloric effects─thermal changes induced by applied hydrostatic pressure that enable heat to be moved against a temperature gradient. Although several SCO compounds have been reported to display promising barocaloric properties─including high pressure sensitivity, a large entropy change, and minimal transition hysteresis─it is challenging to control the transition temperature of a material without adversely impacting its phase-change behavior. This limitation restricts the scope of thermal applications relevant to a given SCO material. Here, we show how cocrystallization with solid coformers allows the SCO transition of Fe(HB(tz)3)2 (HB(tz)3– = hydrotris(1,2,4-triazol-1-yl)borate) to be manipulated across a wide temperature range. In particular, we report a series of cocrystals with SCO transition temperatures spanning from 185 to 350 K and varying degrees of associated hysteresis and cooperativity. We further establish structure–property relationships between coformer identity and SCO transition behavior through a combination of structural characterization, magnetometry, vibrational spectroscopy, and calorimetry. Notably, two cocrystals feature sharp SCO transitions near 200 K that produce large and highly reversible barocaloric effects in a low-temperature regime that has been difficult to access for most classes of barocaloric materials. More broadly, these results provide new insights into cocrystallization as a generalizable synthetic strategy for systematically tuning the properties of SCO materials.

title: Stereochemical Identity of a Single Fluorosugar Enables Noninvasive Dual-Biomarker Fingerprinting of Cancer
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Clinical molecular imaging of cancer largely relies on single biomarker-attributable readouts. Through an efficient trapping mechanism, 2-[18F]FDG robustly links PET readouts to the Warburg effect, illuminating only a single metabolic axis within the multichannel biochemical network of cancer. The versatile chemical space of synthetic fluorosugars, however, may offer an attractive framework for broadening the repertoire of metabolic markers accessible to noninvasive imaging. Here, we report Fluorine Metabolic Imaging (FMI), a molecular MRI strategy for simultaneous in vivo mapping of two metabolic biomarkers using a single probe. FMI exploits the altered biochemistry of 3-fluoro-3-deoxy-d-galactose (3FDGal), which undergoes orthogonal intracellular redox transformations mediated by ALDH1A1 and AKR1B1, each yielding a stably trapped fluorine-labeled metabolite with a characteristic 19F-NMR peak. Concurrently mapped by 19F-MRI, these two enzyme-attributable readouts enable noninvasive spatially resolved dual-biomarker visualization. We establish the trapping mechanism of 3FDGal and its enzymatic basis, demonstrating that 3FDGal-initiated fingerprints reflect dual-biomarker variations across different cancer cells. In vivo, FMI distinguishes tumors with contrasting metabolic phenotypes, herein demonstrated in human xenografts not detectable by the canonical 2-[18F]FDG-PET approach. Establishing this proof-of-concept platform for noninvasive multilayered tumor subtyping, FMI with fluorosugars extends metabolic imaging beyond the Warburg scheme into unexplored dimensions of cancer diagnostics.

title: Symmetry-breaking induced highly active Ni sites simultaneously trigger interfacial hydrogen-bond network reconstruction for efficient CO2 electroreduction in strong acidic media
source: National Science Review Advance Access
abstract: Electrocatalytic CO2 reduction reaction (CO2RR) in strong acidic media (pH ≤ 2) offers many unique advantages compared to alkaline electrolytes, but it still remains some significant challenges including the competing hydrogen evolution reaction (HER), low selectivity and poor stability. Herein, we report that symmetry-breaking induced highly active Ni sites incorporated within ultrathin covalent organic polymer nanosheets (p-Ni1/2Pc), can simultaneously trigger interfacial hydrogen-bond network reconstruction for efficient acidic CO2RR. Direct visualization via scanning tunneling microscopy (STM) reveals the presence of Ni vacancies and uncoordinated pyrrolic N, which collectively break the local symmetry around Ni sites. This asymmetry not only optimizes the electronic structure of Ni sites to kinetically favor CO2RR over HER, but more importantly, it reconfigures the interfacial hydrogen-bond network via uncoordinated pyrrolic N. The reconstructed hydrogen-bond network effectively restricts proton transfer, while symmetry breaking creates a CO2-enriched local microenvironment. title: Click-Functionalizable Tetrathiafulvalene-Tetrathiolate Diradicaloids as Modular NIR-II Fluorophores
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Near-infrared (NIR) emissive fluorophores are appealing for biological imaging and sensing applications, particularly in the lower-energy NIR-II region (1000–1700 nm). Compared to light in the visible and NIR-I regions, NIR-II light undergoes less absorption and scattering by biological tissues, enabling deeper tissue penetration and higher imaging resolution. Tetrathiafulvalene-tetrathiolate (TTFtt)-bridged bimetallic diradicaloid complexes exhibit bright NIR-II emission with high photoluminescence quantum yields (PLQYs) relative to other NIR-II fluorophores. These complexes are also particularly modular, as the capping ligands on the metal centers can be substituted to impart desired properties. Here, azide-functionalized bis(imino)acenaphthene (BIAN) capping ligands are introduced to leverage and expand this modularity. BIAN-capped TTFtt complexes exhibit chemical and photophysical properties comparable to previously reported TTFtt complexes. BIAN backbones functionalized with an azide group further enable Huisgen cycloaddition “click” chemistry for the attachment of diverse functional moieties while preserving the intrinsic NIR-II photophysical properties of the TTFtt core. As one example, a sulfonate-clicked TTFtt complex (1-C3) displays enhanced solubility and increased photoluminescence (PL) intensity in aqueous solutions compared to other TTFtt complexes. Notably, 1-C3 also exhibits pH-dependent PL intensity, suggesting its potential utility as an NIR-II-emitting pH sensor. Furthermore, the enhanced water solubility of 1-C3 enabled us to obtain in vivo gastrointestinal imaging in murine models. Overall, these results demonstrate the dramatically expanded modularity of TTFtt complexes through the use of clickable-BIAN ligands.

title: Reaction‐Programmed Dual‐State Molecular Engineering Decouples Mechanical Reinforcement and Ion Transport for Durable Flexible Zinc Devices
source: Advanced Energy Materials
abstract: ABSTRACT Flexible aqueous zinc‐ion batteries demand hydrogel electrolytes that simultaneously reconcile mechanical durability, fast ion transport, and stable electrode/electrolyte interfaces. Yet abundant polar groups in conventional polyacrylamide hydrogels strongly coordinate Zn 2+ , creating an intrinsic trade‐off between network reinforcement and ionic mobility. Here, we report a reaction‐programmed bound‐free dual‐state molecular engineering strategy using acetylurea to orchestrate the polymer network, Zn 2+ coordination, and aqueous microenvironment. Initially, acetylurea acts as a molecular patch, reacting with polyacrylamide through Schiff‐base chemistry to form a dynamic imine‐crosslinked network that reinforces interchain coupling while shielding excessive Zn 2+ trapping. The optimized hydrogel thus sustains 6100% fracture strain while retaining near‐liquid ionic conductivity (19.1 mS cm −1 ). After reactive sites approach saturation, free acetylurea reconstructs the Zn 2+ solvation sheath and hydrogen‐bond network, lowers water activity, accelerates desolvation, and homogenizes interfacial Zn 2+ flux. This cooperative regulation suppresses dendrites and parasitic reactions, enabling highly reversible Zn plating/stripping. Zn||Zn symmetric cells cycle for over 10 000 h, while Zn||MnO 2 and Zn||C devices sustain 4000 and 10 000 cycles, respectively, with integrated sensing/electrochemical functions retained after ∼100 000 bending cycles. This molecular program decouples mechanical reinforcement from ion transport across fundamentally distinct intercalation and capacitive charge‐storage mechanisms, establishing a general design principle for durable, deformable aqueous electrochemical systems.

title: Metal-oxo clusters stabilize electron-selective interfaces for efficient perovskite solar cells
source: Joule
abstract: Efficient perovskite photovoltaics require durable interfaces compatible with scalable manufacturing. Solution-processable metal-oxo clusters combine robust inorganic frameworks with tunable organic components to enhance charge extraction and suppress ion migration. Complementary clusters stabilize both interfaces of the electron-transport layer, enabling a certified efficiency of 26.7% and improved operational stability. This modular strategy links molecular interface engineering with scalable coating, offering a pathway toward efficient, durable perovskite solar technologies.

title: Liquid-Phase Deep Carbon Elongation from C1 to Crystalline Graphite
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Wet-chemical synthesis of well extended sp2-carbon from simple carbon feedstocks under mild solution-phase conditions remains a longstanding challenge due to the stringent requirements of reversible C–C coupling and error-correcting aromatization. Here, we show that a Lewis-acid-assisted triflic acid medium, TfOH/Hg(OTf)2, promotes the direct conversion of chloromethane solvents into condensed hydrocarbon products and even into crystalline graphitic flakes in a one-pot solution synthesis. GC–MS, time-resolved MALDI-TOF mass spectrometry, nuclear magnetic resonance, and Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy experiments reveal the spontaneous establishment of a dynamic hydrocarbon pool. Within this pool, short-chain hydrocarbon intermediates from early C–C coupling were observed and evolved into highly branched alkanes and polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) ensembles prior to the precipitation of crystalline graphitic solids. Raman, transmission electron microscopy, and angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy measurements confirm the graphitic crystallinity and linear Dirac band dispersion of the isolated flakes. This work demonstrates that the dual-acid system can drive continuous carbon–carbon coupling and consecutive C(sp3)-C(sp2) hybridization transitions, overcoming kinetic barriers that conventionally require pyrolytic temperatures.

title: Spiroselenopyrans: Reversible Light- and Soft-Acid-Triggered Switching of Spirocyclic C–Se Bonds
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Spiropyrans (SPs) are among the most exploited molecular scaffolds for photoswitching. Despite the potential of heavy chalcogen substitution at the spiro site to reshape bond characteristics and unlock distinct functionalities, SP analogs with chalcogens heavier than sulfur remain underexplored. Herein, we report the rational design and synthesis of spiroselenopyrans (SSPs), an emerging family of selenium-centered photoswitches, using steric hindrance engineering to suppress undesired benzoselenophene cyclization, a strategy that readily yields diversely substituted SSP derivatives. Compared with oxygen/sulfur-centered counterparts, the elongated, low-energy C–Se bond and narrowed HOMO–LUMO gap of SSPs enable efficient and accelerated photoisomerization to the trans-planar ring-opened selenomerocyanine (SMC). Notably, SSPs exhibit distinctive selectivity for soft acids, undergoing spontaneous ring-opening upon binding to Ag+ to form a cis-nonplanar Ag+-SMC complex while remaining inert toward hard protons. This work establishes SSPs as robust dual-responsive switches, broadens the chemical space of SP chemistry, and paves the way for advanced multistimuli-responsive molecular systems.

title: Bandedge-State-Limited Single-Photon Emission from Volumetric Quantum Design of 2D Colloidal Quantum Wells
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Present-day solution-processable single-photon sources are dominated by three-dimensionally confined colloidal quantum emitters, yet their particle-to-particle variation in single-exciton properties limits reproducibility and scalability. Here, to avoid such heterogeneity, we demonstrate reliable room-temperature single-photon emission from atomically flat two-dimensional (2D) colloidal quantum wells (CQWs) with inherently uniform one-dimensional quantum confinement, despite their long-standing limitations of efficient multiexciton emission and pronounced exciton-surface susceptibility. We resolve these challenges through volumetric quantum design (VQD) of CQWs, yielding a highly localized, single bandedge state. This design laterally confines the bandedge excitonic domain within the exciton coherent area and vertically decouples it from surface states via a thick, strain-relieved quantum-barrier shell that preserves strong confinement, overcoming the daunting thickness-confinement trade-off in 2D CQWs. Statistical single-particle spectroscopy reveals that VQD-CQWs deliver near-blinking-free (on-time: >99.5%) and fluence-insensitive antibunching (g(2)(0): ∼0.041), protected by a bandedge-state-filling bottleneck, together with linear polarization of up to 73% under cavity-free conditions, originating from synergistic transition-dipole and electric-field anisotropies. These advances establish 2D CQWs as a viable, homogeneous and scalable platform for quantum technologies.

title: Sulfurization Breaking the Ferroelectric Polarization Bottleneck in PbTiO3
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Robust ferroelectricity is crucial for high-performance ferroelectric nonvolatile memories. PbTiO3 (PTO) is expected to show large polarization with a high Curie temperature (TC). However, the inherent leakage current of PTO limits its actual ferroelectricity. To address this limitation, we prepare PTO films via sulfurization using a cost-effective sol–gel method. The pristine PTO films show notable remnant polarization (Pr) of 61.6 μC/cm2 with well-saturated electric field–polarization loops that have not been achieved in either bulk or thin-film forms previously. Upon sulfurization, Pr increases to approximately 180% of its pristine value, rising from 61.6 to 111.7 μC/cm2 alongside a moderate coercive field of 697 kV/cm, rendering the films competitive among currently reported large polarization ferroelectrics (Pr > 100 μC/cm2). Additionally, an elevated TC of up to 526 °C was observed in sulfurized PTO films, compared with 505 °C for pristine PTO thin films. First-principles calculations reveal that the sulfur-associated enhancement of tetragonal distortion substantially reduces the short-range restoring interaction, thereby shifting the balance between short-range and long-range forces toward a stronger polar instability; phase-field simulations further reproduce the enhanced ferroelectric polarization. Our study demonstrates an effective sulfurization method for achieving large ferroelectricity, holding great potential for ferroelectric devices.

title: Macrocycle 2D COF Single Crystal
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract We report the synthesis of a two-dimensional (2D) covalent organic framework (COF) single crystal, termed COF-900, constructed from a geminiarene-type macrocycle linker, biphenyl-extended pillar[3]arene containing nine phenyl units. The atomically accurate structure was resolved by three-dimensional electron diffraction (3D ED) of the 2D COF single crystal with a resolution of 1.2 Å, unveiling the conformation of the macrocycle in the layered backbone as well as AB interlayer stacking. The macrocycle exhibits a similar stacking mode in both the COF and the molecular crystal of the linker, suggesting prealignment of linkers during COF crystal growth through a mechanism termed alignment-led framework assembly (ALFA). Cryo-transmission electron microscopy images further provided direct real-space visualization of the macrocycle, where three types of interconnected pores were clearly visualized with sizes of 1.1, 1.5, and 2.3 nm.

title: Multitime Scale Operando Kinetic Decoupling of Photogenerated Carriers
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The energy-conversion efficiency of photoelectrochemical (PEC) systems is governed by photogenerated charge-carrier kinetics that span several orders of magnitude, from subpicosecond generation in the semiconductor bulk to millisecond consumption at catalytic surfaces. This vast temporal disparity severs the causal link between ultrafast carrier events and steady-state photocurrents, leaving the mechanistic origins of efficiency losses speculative and fundamentally hindering the rational optimization of PEC devices. Here, we bridge this gap by integrating multitime scale operando spectroscopies, ranging from transient absorption to electrochemical measurements, on model β-Fe2O3 photoanodes. This approach enables deconvolution of the temporal evolution of photogenerated carriers into distinct signatures attributable to bulk diffusion, charge accumulation, and catalytic-intermediate formation, thereby decoupling and identifying the dynamic fingerprints of carriers within a champion β-Fe2O3 photoanode. These fingerprints establish a mechanistic framework that directly connects multitime scale carrier dynamics and kinetics to the design principles of high-performance photoelectrodes, transforming the understanding of and approach to engineering solar water splitting systems.

title: Small-Molecule Activation Reshapes the Catalytic Conformational Landscape during Ca2+ ATPase Turnover
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Understanding how small molecules enhance enzymatic turnover is a central challenge in chemical biology because activation arises from redistribution of transient populations that are difficult to resolve during catalysis. By integrating time-resolved X-ray solution scattering, molecular dynamics simulations, and kinetic modeling, we determine how the small-molecule activator yakuchinone A modulates the catalytic cycle of the sarco/endoplasmic reticulum Ca2+ ATPase (SERCA), a prototypical P-type ATPase. We show that the activator accelerates the catalytic cycle by reshaping the conformational landscape during turnover, with a disproportionate enhancement of late-cycle transitions. This kinetic modulation of the rate-limiting step increases the population of Ca2+-bound E2P states, while significantly reducing accumulation of Ca2+-free E2*Pi transient states associated with dephosphorylation. Ensemble-based structural models quantitatively reproduce the experimental scattering profiles and support redistribution of conformational populations during turnover. Together, these findings provide a time-resolved mechanistic picture of how small molecules enhance enzymatic turnover through redistribution of conformational populations and selective acceleration of rate-limiting transitions.

title: Buried Interfacial Transport Governs Oxide-Protected Electrocatalysis
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Protective overlayers are widely used to stabilize metal catalysts under harsh electrochemical conditions. Unlike graphene coatings, oxide overlayers introduce a buried metal-oxide interface that fundamentally reshapes reaction pathways by separating proton delivery from product release. Although proton transport through oxides has been extensively investigated, the fate of reaction products at buried interfaces remains unresolved; for example, H2-molecule vs H-atom pathways remain under debate in oxide-protected hydrogen evolution. Here, we revisit this buried interface using a microelectrochemical cell with well-defined model structures. Systematic measurements across nine metal-oxide heterostructures, combined with density functional theory calculations, reveal that product transport is governed by two sequential kinetic barriers: hydrogen spillover across the metal-oxide junction and hydrogen permeation through the oxide lattice. These coupled barriers determine whether reaction products are released, accumulate at buried interfaces, or induce interfacial failure. This work not only identifies superior Pt-TiO2 and Pd-TiO2 but also clarifies which step is impeded in Au-TiO2, Pt-SiO2, Pt-HfO2, Pd-SiO2, Pd-HfO2, Au-SiO2, and Au-HfO2 heterostructures. Guided by these model studies, we implement a TiO2 protection strategy in a proton-exchange-membrane water electrolyzer with remarkable durability. These findings provide a framework for constructing a complete proton-to-product route for buried interfaces, potentially resolving long-standing ambiguities in oxide-protected electrocatalysis.

title: Energy poverty in an era of geopolitical instability: The role of Chinese FDI and south–south cooperation in Africa
source: ScienceDirect Publication: Energy Policy
abstract: The rising geopolitical fragmentation, driven by geopolitical tensions, conflicts and wars, has reshaped the global energy landscape, increasing uncertainty and vulnerability in energy markets. These disruptions present serious challenges for different economies in the Global South, where countries already face significant difficulties in facilitating energy transition and mitigating energy poverty. In this context, South-South cooperation may represent an important tool to address energy challenges, particularly through foreign investment. This study investigates the contribution of Chinese FDI to reducing energy poverty in Africa through different channels and whether conflict conditions influence the extent to which Chinese FDI contributes to improving energy outcomes. Our study contributes to the literature on the role of Chinese foreign capital in reducing energy poverty in Africa by examining both the underlying mechanisms and the potential role of conflict conditions in shaping these effects. To empirically explore this complex nexus, we rely on Structural Equation Modelling using a set of energy and socioeconomic variables from 2005 to 2022. The findings reveal a significant positive association between Chinese FDI and energy performance, with the prosperity channel representing the main mechanism. This association appears weaker in conflict-affected contexts, suggesting that geopolitical stability conditions the extent to which foreign investment is associated with improved energy outcomes. Policymakers in the region should consider creating a more attractive and stable investment environment to promote trade ties with Chinese companies, as these ties could be used as a tool to alleviate energy poverty.

title: The missing dimension of European energy sovereignty: The geopolitics of market infrastructure
source: ScienceDirect Publication: Energy Policy
abstract: European energy-security analysis has focused mainly on physical supply. This paper examines a less-examined dimension of European energy sovereignty: exposure to the mechanisms through which prices are formed, risks are managed and uncertainty is transmitted across interconnected markets. We distinguish physical dependence on a fuel from exposure to its price, and argue that the combination of weather-driven renewable variability, gas prices and carbon prices is closer to a Keynesian uncertainty than to a sum of insurable risks: their relationships are unstable, policy responses alter the rules of price formation, and hedging can turn price risk into liquidity risk. Nordic annual day-ahead prices for 2015–2025 illustrate the mechanism. In 2022, southern Norway (NO2) and southern Sweden (SE4), with almost no gas-fired generation, averaged €211/MWh and €152/MWh, against €24/MWh (NO4) and €59/MWh (SE1) in the north. This suggests that exposure depends on interconnection and congestion more than on national generation mix, although annual data cannot separate these from hydrology and nuclear availability. Norway and Sweden have since politically responded to this shock by postponing or withdrawing new interconnector investment. We then examine the infrastructure of price formation: Germany's retention of a single bidding zone despite the 2025 Bidding Zone Review, and the concentration of trading, clearing and benchmark functions across electricity, gas and carbon markets notably around EEX Group and ICE. We argue that limiting and distributing this uncertainty, rather than eliminating it, deserves treatment as a dimension of European energy sovereignty alongside security of physical supply.

title: The emerging geopolitics of sustainable aviation fuel: Policy architectures, book-and-claim and european strategic dependencies
source: ScienceDirect Publication: Energy Policy
abstract: Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF) is becoming a strategic component of aviation decarbonization, but its expansion depends on technological, economic, institutional, and resource conditions. This study compares the combinations of policy instruments, structural production characteristics, and market-governance arrangements observed in the European Union, the United States, the United Kingdom, Japan, Singapore, and Brazil, and considers the potential strategic vulnerabilities these configurations suggest, particularly for the European Union. The comparative qualitative policy analysis draws on peer-reviewed literature, legislation, regulatory documents, and institutional sources, organized through a single four-part framework: policy-instrument mix; structural production conditions; market and governance conditions; and potential strategic vulnerabilities. The cases display different configurations. The European Union and the United Kingdom emphasize mandatory demand; the United States relies more heavily on producer incentives; Japan and Singapore emphasize coordination and supply security; and Brazil combines established biofuel capabilities with a developing SAF framework. These observations do not identify causal effects or rank the configurations. Instead, they indicate possible exposure to feedstock, production, finance, policy-continuity, import, and certification constraints. Book-and-Claim is examined as a governance arrangement that separates environmental attributes from physical fuel flows; its practical contribution depends on credible certification, verification, registry governance, and interoperability. For the European Union, the comparison suggests that regulatory leadership may coexist with external supply and institutional dependencies. The concept of resilient interdependence is therefore proposed as a policy lens rather than a measured outcome.

title: Decarbonising industrial hydrogen supply systems under EU taxonomy regulation: A multi-objective decision-support framework for existing facilities
source: ScienceDirect Publication: Applied Energy
abstract: Hydrogen is a crucial vector for decarbonising hard-to-abate industrial sectors, but its deployment increasingly depends on regulatory sustainability criteria alongside economic performance. In Europe, frameworks such as the EU Taxonomy and RED II impose life cycle emission thresholds that directly influence hydrogen system design. This work proposes a flexible multi-objective mixed-integer linear programming framework for the design of lowcarbon hydrogen supply systems for industrial applications. The model integrates renewable and biogenic resources, electricity generation, hydrogen production technologies, inter-monthly hydrogen storage, and resource-specific transport. Economic performance and life cycle CO2eq emissions are optimised simultaneously by using an augmented epsilon-constraint method, while regulatory sustainability thresholds are assessed a posteriori. Water consumption is explicitly included, enabling analysis in regions were water scarcity constraints production. The framework is applied to western Andalusia (Spain) and the Republic of Ireland, which differ in resource availability and hydrogen demand. Regional resource-to-demand ratios strongly shape Pareto front structures and technology portfolios. Biomass gasification emerges as the most cost-effective pathway in resource-abundant settings, while electrolytic routes dominate in resource-constrained regions. All Pareto-optimal solutions comply with the EU Taxonomy emission threshold, although the economic cost of compliance differs between regions. Overall, the framework provides a transparent and adaptable decision-support tool for assessing cost-emission trade-offs and regulatory compliance in regional hydrogen planning. It supports the development of context-specific, policy-consistent hydrogen roadmaps that balance economic competitiveness, environmental performance, and sustainability requirements.
