title: Synergistic Bimolecular Reconstruction of the Perovskite‐Carbon Interface Enables 23.6%‐Efficiency Fully Printable Mesoscopic Perovskite Solar Cells
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Hole‐conductor‐free, fully printable mesoscopic perovskite solar cells (p‐MPSCs) hold compelling promise for photovoltaic industrialization. However, their power conversion efficiency (PCE) remains constrained by limited hole collection at the perovskite‐carbon interface. Here, we introduce a synergistic bimolecular post‐treatment using toluene diisocyanate (TDI) and 4‐methyl sulfonyl phenyl methylammonium chloride (MSBH) to reconstruct this critical interface. We demonstrate that TDI reacts with surface formamidinium to polish and activate the perovskite terminations, while MSBH subsequently grafts onto this activated surface. This combined action simultaneously reconstructs the interface with optimized surface energy band bending and minimized interfacial defects, thereby facilitating hole extraction and suppressing non‐radiative recombination. Consequently, this strategy elevates the PCE of small‐area p‐MPSCs (0.1 cm 2 ) to 23.6%. Furthermore, it enables the fabrication of a p‐MPSC minimodule with an active area of 52.7 cm 2 , achieving a PCE of 22.1%, among the highest values ever reported for carbon‐based, fully printable architectures. Devices retained 98% of their initial PCE after 750 h of operational stability testing at 55°C ± 5°C. This work provides an effective interface reconstruction strategy that concurrently addresses defect passivation and energy alignment, paving the way for high‐performance, stable, and scalable cost‐effective perovskite photovoltaics.

title: High‐Density Colossal Barocaloric Effect in Quasi‐Spherical Ionic Plastic Crystal (Et4N)(CrO3Cl)
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT The barocaloric effect driven by hydrostatic pressure of solid‐state phase transition materials is regarded as one of the means to replace traditional vapor compression refrigeration technology due to its environmental friendliness and high efficiency. However, the refrigeration density of the currently reported solid‐state barocaloric refrigerants is generally low, which is not conducive to the low cost and miniaturization of refrigeration equipment. In order to solve this problem, we explore the barocaloric effect of ionic plastic crystal (Et 4 N)(CrO 3 Cl), which shows a high refrigeration density due to weak hydrogen bond interaction, quasi‐spherical structure, and large volume change during the first‐order phase transition. Under a driving pressure of 100 MPa, the reversible isothermal entropy changes (Δ S it, rev ) per unit mass and per unit volume are 284.1 J kg −1 K −1 and 0.397 J cm −3 K −1 , respectively. Regardless of the evaluation from any perspective, this refrigerant shows a high refrigeration density. In addition, (Et 4 N)(CrO 3 Cl) shows relatively high‐pressure sensitivity (). This also enables it to exhibit excellent refrigeration capacity (RC = 3636 J kg −1 = 5.08 J cm −3 ) at a relatively low pressure (100 MPa). The discovery of this high‐density barocaloric refrigerant will help to promote the research on the miniaturization of refrigeration equipment.

title: Sequential Regulation of Dendrite Initiation and Propagation for High‐Current Hydroborate‐Based Solid‐State Sodium Metal Batteries
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Hydroborate solid electrolytes (SEs) offer fast Na + transport, low density, and compatibility with Na metal, yet their current tolerance is restricted by dendrite‐induced short circuits in all‐solid‐state Na metal batteries (ASSNBs). Here, a spatially coordinated dual‐interlayer architecture is developed to regulate dendrite initiation and propagation in Na 4 B 10 H 10 B 12 H 12 (NBH)‐based ASSNBs. At the Na|NBH interface, a three‐dimensional Sn/C framework enables Na infiltration into the porous scaffold and homogenizes current distribution, while dynamically formed Na–Sn sites facilitate Na + transport and redistribution, thereby maintaining intimate interfacial contact and suppressing dendrite initiation. Within the NBH SE, a Na 2.9375 PS 3.9375 Cl 0.0625 (NPSC) sulfide interlayer reacts with penetrating Na to suppress dendrite propagation, with crack‐like pathways terminating near the NBH|NPSC interface. This sequential regulation increases the critical current density from 0.5 to 3.3 mA cm −2 . Symmetric cells operate stably for 7000 and 1000 h at 0.5 and 3.0 mA cm −2 , respectively. Full cells with an O3‐type NaNi 1/3 Fe 1/3 Mn 1/3 O 2 cathode retain 75% capacity after 800 cycles at 2 C, while supporting cathode loadings up to 15 mg cm −2 . This work establishes sequential control of dendrite initiation and propagation as a design principle for high‐current hydroborate‐based ASSNBs.

title: Flexible 2D Donor‐Acceptor MOFs Enable Tunable and Pressure‐Responsive TSCT–TADF for Heterocrystal Photonic Logic
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Efficient thermally activated delayed fluorescence (TADF) materials that combine high efficiency, color tunability, and dynamic stimulus responsiveness are highly desirable for adaptive photonic technologies, yet remain difficult to realize within a single crystalline platform. Here, flexible two‐dimensional (2D) donor‐acceptor (D–A) metal‐organic frameworks (MOFs) are developed through integrating an aggregation‐induced‐emission‐active triphenylamine donor with size‐matched electron‐deficient acceptors. Solvent‐directed assembly, donor conformational flexibility, and acceptor electronic modulation cooperatively regulate the D–A packing and through‐space charge‐transfer (TSCT) effect. The resulting MOFs exhibit broadly tunable TADF emission (474–635 nm), delayed lifetimes (0.11–7.65 µs), and photoluminescence quantum yields (PLQY, 0.52%–74.24%). Relative to the DMF‐derived structures, the DMA‐derived MOFs display increases of up to 51‐fold in delayed lifetime and 6‐fold in PLQY, while calculations support an unconventional high‐lying reverse intersystem crossing (hRISC) pathway. More importantly, the structural adaptability of the layered frameworks enables pressure‐induced reconfiguration of D–A interactions, giving rise to reversible piezochromic TSCT–TADF with emission shifts of up to 113 nm. A multicomponent heterocrystal is further constructed to translate pressure‐dependent emission changes into optical logic operations. These results establish flexible 2D D–A MOFs as a dynamic platform for integrating efficient TADF, mechanical responsiveness, and heterocrystal photonic functionality.

title: Reconceptualizing Thermal Runaway Mechanisms in Sulfide Solid‐State Batteries via Dynamic Interfacial Reconstruction
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT The commercialization of sulfide‐based all‐solid‐state batteries (ASSBs) is often predicated on their perceived “intrinsic safety”. However, recent evidence of violent thermal runaway under abuse conditions has shattered this consensus, revealing a sobering gap in our mechanistic understanding of solid‐state failure. In this Perspective, we argue that the current stagnation in safety research stems from a “liquid‐legacy” mindset that fails to account for the unique solid–solid reactive landscape. We propose that the thermal failure of sulfide ASSBs is fundamentally governed by a dynamic interfacial reconstruction involving the continuous electrochemical and chemo‐mechanical evolution of the interphase during cycling. By deconstructing the staged thermochemical cascade, we demonstrate how cycling‐induced metastable species, such as polysulfides and mixed‐conducting interphases, act as reactive “pre‐conditioners” that dictate failure pathways. This framework explains long‐standing experimental inconsistencies, including divergent SO 2 evolution profiles and fluctuating trigger temperatures across identical material couples. This shift from a static material‐centric view to a dynamic interface‐centric framework reframes the rational design of truly robust, next‐generation energy storage systems.

title: Interfacial Electronic Reconstruction Activates TiO2 in MnO2/TiO2 Heterostructures for Accelerated Sulfur Redox Chemistry
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Lithium–sulfur batteries are promising for next‐generation energy storage but are limited by sluggish sulfur redox kinetics originating from insufficient regulation of interfacial electronic structures. Here, we report a MnO 2 /TiO 2 heterostructure with integrated interfacial bonding, in which residual carbon is inherently incorporated into the interfacial region. The characterizations reveal pronounced reconstruction of the local coordination and electronic environment upon heterostructure formation, including Ti─O─Mn bonding, reduced Ti states, and substantial changes in the surface potential and valence‐band structure. DFT calculations suggest that the reconstructed interface involves the coexistence of net intercomponent charge redistribution and localized bond polarization, with residual carbon contributing to interfacial electronic coupling. Consistent with this reconstructed electronic environment, Ti‐derived sites exhibit enhanced electronic response toward polysulfides, while MnO 2 and residual carbon contribute to the coupled interfacial structure. Consequently, MnO 2 /TiO 2 catalyst enables stable cycling under a high sulfur loading of 9.2 mg cm −2 and, when integrated as a functional interlayer, allows the sulfur cathode to deliver a high specific capacity of 1569 mAh g −1 together with durability over 1000 cycles, with a capacity decay rate of 0.054% per cycle. This work highlights chemically integrated oxide heterointerfaces as an effective platform for regulating local electronic structures and accelerating sulfur redox chemistry.

title: Spatiotemporally Controlled Lithium Delivery via a Graphene‐Hydrogel System for Wnt Activation and Spinal Cord Repair
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Wnt signaling plays essential roles in neural development and has significant potential to promote regeneration after central nervous system (CNS) injury. However, therapeutic strategies that locally modulate Wnt signaling in vivo remain limited. Herein, we develop a battery‐inspired graphene‐lithium hydrogel (GLH) that enables sustained, controllable delivery of lithium ions (Li + ) to injury sites. Li + inhibits glycogen synthase kinase 3β (GSK3β), activating pro‐regenerative Wnt/β‐catenin signaling. Beyond Wnt activation, GLH provides complementary therapeutic functions: oxidation of lithium (0) attenuates reactive oxygen species‐associated stress, while the gelatin‐based hydrogel matrix supplies a permissive extracellular matrix (ECM)‐like niche. In co‐cultures of human‐induced pluripotent stem cell‐derived neural progenitor cells and macrophages, GLH suppresses pro‐inflammatory signaling and enhances neurogenesis. In a murine spinal cord injury complete transection model, a single GLH injection sustains Wnt activation for over one week, reduces acute neuroinflammation and astroglial/fibrotic scarring, and promotes long‐term tissue preservation and functional recovery. Transcriptomic and protein analyses further support coordinated modulation of Wnt‐related, redox, inflammatory, and ECM‐remodeling pathways, accompanying improved locomotor and bladder function and reduced neuropathic pain. Given the conserved role of Wnt signaling in regeneration, the GLH offers a multifunctional materials platform with potential applicability beyond the CNS.

title: Topological‐Insulator‐Based Ion‐Electron‐Coupled Nanochannels With a Photothermally Induced Thermoelectric Field for Enhanced Ionic Transport
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Efficient ion transport is essential for high‐performance energy storage and conversion, yet strong ion–channel interactions in conventional highly polar nanochannels can increase migration barriers and impede rapid ion motion. Here, we report layered ion‐electron‐coupled Bi 2 Te 3 /Ti 3 C 2 T x nanochannels, in which ion transport is synergistically regulated by highly polar interfaces, highly conductive surface states, and a photothermally induced thermoelectric field. The polar MXene interfaces support selective ion transport, whereas the highly conductive surface states of Bi 2 Te 3 enhance interfacial electronic responsiveness, facilitating charge equilibration and mitigating local charge accumulation during ion migration. This interfacial coupling reduces the ion‐transport activation energy to 8.02 kJ mol −1 , 34.6% lower than that of pristine MXene nanochannels. As a functional demonstration of enhanced ion transport, the nanochannels deliver a 5.56‐fold increase in osmotic power density (18.9 W m −2 ) under a 50‐fold NaCl concentration gradient. Upon illumination, the photothermally induced temperature gradient activates the Seebeck response of Bi 2 Te 3 , providing an additional thermoelectric driving force for directional ion migration, as reflected by a further increase in power density to 25.5 W m −2 . This work provides a strategy for enhancing ion transport under nanoconfinement through interfacial‐electronic‐coupling‐mediated regulation and thermoelectric‐field‐assisted driving.

title: Halide Perovskite Heterojunction Crossbar Arrays for Selector‐Free Analog In‐Memory Computing
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Passive memristor crossbars require each cell to suppress sneak‐path currents while retaining gradual, reproducible conductance programmability. In halide perovskites, however, sneak‐current suppression and analog programmability have rarely been integrated and validated across passive arrays. Fabricated arrays have typically relied on peripheral circuitry to mitigate parasitic currents, whereas self‐rectifying analog memristors have largely remained at the single‐device level. Here, a discrete three‐dimensional/two‐dimensional (3D/2D) FAPbI 3 /BDAPbI 4 heterojunction, formed through controlled in situ conversion, is shown to integrate diode‐like rectification and analog resistive switching within a single, nominally symmetric Au/perovskite/Au cell. The 3D perovskite enables field‐assisted ion migration, while the 2D perovskite introduces an interfacial barrier that induces asymmetric transport, resulting in intrinsic rectification and stable analog switching. A 32 × 32 passive crossbar array comprising 1024 cells, fabricated on silicon below 150°C, exhibits a 99.4% functional‐device yield, a synaptic nonlinearity of 0.007, and stable operation over 640 000 programming pulses. Cell‐resolved measurements demonstrate analog image programming and erasing, and a tiled‐array inference model incorporating the measured cell characteristics and electrical nonidealities connects the experimentally realized array to in‐memory‐computing performance. These results establish chemically defined perovskite heterojunctions as a low‐temperature, silicon‐compatible materials strategy for selector‐free analog in‐memory computing.

title: Ultrarobust and Thermo‐Mechano‐Photo‐Responsive Elastomers by Supramolecular and Dynamic 3D Topological Architectures
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Mechanically robust elastomers are being widely used in multi‐stimuli‐responsive systems including closed‐loop recycling, information encryption, and advanced photolithography. However, their advancement is hindered by an inherent trade‐off: structural integrity for mechanical robustness versus molecular‐level reversibility for stimuli responsiveness. In this study, we constructed ultrarobust recyclable and photo‐responsive supramolecular‐dynamic covalent networks (SDCN) based on molecular engineering of anthracene‐functionalized poly(urethane‐urea‐amide) (PUUA) networks with hindered urea motifs. Well‐designed SDCN achieves multiscale assembly through coordinated π–π stacking, hydrogen bonding, and dynamic covalent interactions, creating dynamic coupling between soft‐chain crosslinks and self‐assembly hard domains, and driving microphase separation. Under stretching, strain‐activated disassembly of dynamically assembled nanostructures synergizes with stress‐induced crystallization, in situ evolving three‐dimensional topological architectures and promoting strength‐toughness enhancement. Consequently, PUUA elastomers exhibit remarkable mechanical performance (100.17 MPa tensile strength, 1286.79% elongation and 498.15 MJ m −3 toughness at room temperature; 113.67 MPa strength and 667.8% elongation at −40°C) and recycling performance (92.4% recyclability via solvent reprocessing). Significantly, UV‐responsive anthracene photonic moieties combined with temperature‐mediated interfacial SDCN transition enable fluorescent encryption and sub‐micron photolithographic patterning. Therefore, this work coordinates dynamic thermal‐mechanical‐optical responses and multi‐scale molecular transition mechanisms, which can be expected to boost high‐precision photolithographic patterning and flexible microcircuit printing fields.

title: 3D‐Printable Bioinspired Heterostructured Polymer With Exceptional Toughness and Fatigue Resistance
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Polymeric materials are widely used in load‐bearing biomedical applications, yet achieving concurrent high fracture toughness and fatigue resistance remains a longstanding challenge due to their intrinsic trade‐off. Here, we propose a bioinspired heterostructure (BIHS) fatigue‐resistant strategy inspired by the material‐structure synergy of natural intervertebral discs (IVDs). The optimized BIHS composite achieves a fracture toughness of 1252 ± 70.13 kJ/m 2 and a fatigue threshold of 8010 J/m 2 , outperforming conventional polymer materials. The BIHS enables stress redistribution at crack tips and activates multiple energy‐dissipation pathways, including crack bridging and deflection, fiber pull‐out and rupture, and interfacial interactions, thereby suppressing crack initiation and propagation under cyclic loading. Leveraging this design, we further develop a BIHS‐IVD that withstands 1.5 × 10 7 cycles without failure under physiological loading in saline conditions, corresponding to an estimated 45‐year cycle‐equivalent fatigue life. These results establish a generalizable bioinspired design framework for durable polymeric materials and provide a promising pathway toward long‐lasting biomedical implants.

title: Orthogonal Self‐Assembled Two‐Dimensional Charge‐Transfer Cocrystals With Superior Photothermal Stability for Low‐Loss NIR‐II Waveguiding and Epitaxial Heterostructure Fabrication
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Low‐dimensional organic near‐infrared (NIR) crystals hold tremendous potential for integrated photonics. However, simultaneously achieving two‐dimensional (2D) structural growth and low‐loss waveguiding within the NIR‐II region remains a formidable challenge due to one‐dimensional (1D) packing tendencies imposed by strong charge transfer (CT) interactions. In this study, we strategically choose the extended π‐conjugated structure donor dithieno[2,3‐d:2',3'‐d']benzo[1,2‐b:4,5‐b']dithiophene and the strong electron‐withdrawing acceptor tetracyanoquinodimethane, and report the first large‐scale preparation of 2D organic CT cocrystal microsheets with NIR‐II emission at 1050 nm via a gas‐phase self‐assembly. The strategically expanded conjugation framework not only further promotes the luminescence red‐shift but also introduces an interaction network with orthogonal directions, counterbalancing the intrinsic 1D stacking constraints brought by the strong CT interactions and guiding the crystals into a thermodynamically stable 2D morphology. The compact network plays a crucial role in endowing the material with exceptional structural and photothermal stability, as well as low‐loss optical waveguiding. Furthermore, attributed to the extremely low lattice‐mismatch rate, 1D‐2D branched heterostructures were constructed, which demonstrated efficient energy transfer (ET) and cross‐band optical signal conversion over 600 nm. This work breaks new ground in extending 2D organic cocrystals into the NIR‐II region and provides a promising material platform for low‐loss, and integrated NIR optoelectronic devices.

title: π‑Conjugated Helical Polymer for Circularly Polarized Photodetection and Secure Optoelectronic Encoding
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Helical polymers are promising materials for circularly polarized light (CPL) detection and hardware‐level information security owing to their tunable chiroptical properties, efficient charge transport, and intrinsic conformational randomness. However, designing helical polymers with high chiroptical activity, which can be effectively translated intohigh‐performance CPL detection remains challenging. Herein, we reported the helical polymer, ( SSSS )‐diPDI‐C8‐T‐T, in which point chirality was effectively transferred to π‐extended diperylene diimide (diPDI) backbone. Compared with non‐helical polymer ( SS )‐PDI‐C8‐T‐T, ( SSSS )‐diPDI‐C8‐T‐T exhibited chiroptical activity (the absorption dissymmetry factors, g abs = −1.4 × 10 −3 at 460 nm) in chloroform (10 −5 M), owing to the optimized electric–magnetic ( µ ‐ m ) transition dipole alignment. CPL detectors based on ( SSSS )‐diPDI‐C8‐T‐T annealed thin films exhibited higher average photocurrent dissymmetry factors ( g ph ) of 0.52 at 535 nm and −1.03 at 405 nm, the latter of which is the highest g ph reported for single‐component chiral polymer‐based CPL detection. The enhanced chirality‐induced spin selectivity (CISS) effect increased the spin polarization to 89.03%, contributing to the higher g ph for ( SSSS )‐diPDI‐C8‐T‐T annealed thin films. Leveraging the dual‐wavelength CPL response of ( SSSS )‐diPDI‐C8‐T‐T annealed thin films and spatial randomness, 5 × 8 CPL‐PUF array enabled optoelectronic fingerprinting, with inter‐ and intra‐Hamming distances of 49.278% and 1.655%, respectively. This work highlights helical polymers for CPL detection and chiral optoelectronic fingerprinting.

title: An Implantable In‐Tube System for Quantitative Precision Vagus Neuromodulation and Feedback of Intestinal Motility
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Electrical vagus neuromodulation of intestinal motility has demonstrated significant clinical utility in the field, where targeting the brain–gut axis can serve as an adjunct in treating intestinal diseases. However, quantitatively understanding vagus‐intestine interoceptive information about real‐time and in situ feedback on intestinal motility under the influence of electrical stimulation parameters is one of the most urgent challenges. Here we propose an implantable closed‐loop system that combines a scalable catheter‐type ionic piezoelectric (in‐tube) sensor as diverse as the gut, a microelectronic chip, an electrical vagus stimulation electrode, and a display interface to realize point‐of‐care precision vagus neuromodulation and feedback of intestinal motility. Owing to the radial gradient hydrogel structure design and stress concentration effect, the in‐tube sensor can simultaneously quantitatively detect and display four key parameters of intestinal motility, including intensity, frequency, duration, and local compression rate, with a high sensitivity of 7.0 mV mmHg −1 and unique pressure–time integral behavior with a time sensitivity of 24.1 mV s −1 , making up for the deficiency of traditional sensors that cannot obtain pressure duration. After implanting the in‐tube sensor in the anatomically challenging intestinal lumen of rabbits, we intuitively show how electrical vagus stimulation affects intestinal motility, which guides the optimal frequency window of 5 ∼ 10 Hz.

title: Ultra‐Strong, Leak‐Proof Bio‐Based Polyurethane Ionic Fibers for Sustainable Smart Wearables
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Artificial intelligence (AI)‐integrated digital flexible devices have been widely used in motion detection. However, the emphasis on sensitivity and response speed often overlooks environmental sustainability. Based on a green‐mechanical‐electrical synergistic design, a polar coordination and chemical confinement strategy is proposed to fabricate an ion‐conductive polyurethane fiber. Specifically, chemical confinement refers to the covalent incorporation of the polymerizable ionic‐liquid component into the polyurethane backbone through its hydroxyl‐functionalized imidazolium moiety. Polar coordination involves reversible Mg 2+ –carbonyl interactions that contribute to mechanical reinforcement and Mg 2+ retention. The resulting fiber exhibits a tensile strength of 52.75 MPa and an elongation at break of 1414%. Meanwhile, the in situ grafted ionic liquid provides an ionic conductivity of 0.209 mS cm −1 . After 120 h of vigorous stirring in water, the Mg concentration in the test medium reached 1.9 ppm, showing limited Mg release under the tested condition. Integrating this fiber into smart fabrics enables full‐body motion monitoring and accurate recognition of complex movements with 100% accuracy. This study establishes a closed‐loop paradigm from sustainable molecular design to AI‐driven decision‐making, offering new material design insights for next‐generation green, safe, and high‐performance smart wearable devices.

title: Luminescent and Stable Eu(III) Complex Nanocrystals: A Class of Eu(III) Emitters Toward Amine/Ammonia
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Eu(III) complexes exhibit highly efficient luminescence, while their emissions are significantly sensitive to amine/ammonia‐induced quenching. Herein, we report a class of Eu(III) complex nanocrystals in which aliphatic amines serve as structural regulators to construct highly luminescent and stable ultrasmall Eu(III) emitters. The addition of aliphatic amines enables the originally insoluble complexes to be dissolved in n ‐hexane, producing Eu(III) complex nanocrystal solutions. The primary‐ and secondary‐amine based Eu(btfa) 3 PBI nanocrystal solutions showed photoluminescence quantum yields (PLQYs) reaching 24%–36% and 30%–37%, respectively. In a sharp contrast, the complex's luminescence was completely or substantially quenched when dissolved directly in primary or secondary amine liquids, with PLQYs decreasing to 0 or 0.0%–1.2%. The significantly suppressed quenching upon nanocrystal formation originated from the substantial reduction of vibrationally induced nonradiative decays, which was further supported by the low quenching constants toward amines. The nanocrystal's emission was further enhanced upon using the tertiary amines. A remarkable PLQY of 64% was obtained for tri‐ n ‐decylamine based Eu(dbm) 3 dmbipy nanocrystals. The nanocrystal solutions exhibited excellent stability, with their PLQYs well retained after 10 h of ambient storage or continuous irradiation with 365 nm UV light. Furthermore, proof‐of‐concept experiments demonstrated the potential application of nanocrystal solids as amine/ammonia‐resistant warning labels.

title: Advancements in Multi‐Dimensional Hexagonal Boron Nitride‐Based Thermal Management Materials: A Review
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Hexagonal boron nitride (BN), due to its high thermal conductivity (TC), excellent electrical insulation, and low dielectric constant, has become an ideal filler for designing advanced thermal management materials (TMMs), effectively addressing thermal failure and electromagnetic leakage issues in advanced chips. BN structures in different dimensions (0D, 1D, and 2D) each have their own advantages, their interface morphology directly affects the TC of composite systems. However, there is still a lack of systematic understanding of phonon transport behavior at different interfaces in composite systems and their impact on thermal conduction network construction. This review focuses on dimensional classification and compares the intrinsic TC, phonon transport mechanisms, and network formation behavior of 0D, 1D, and 2D BN fillers. In addition to the traditional filler/polymer interfaces, this analysis also focused on the phonon transport properties at the homogeneous and heterogeneous nanoadditives interfaces of BN. At the same time, the TC of mono‐, di‐, and multi‐component nanoadditives systems were systematically evaluated, revealing the synergistic effects among BN of different dimensions. This review aims to provide a reference for reducing the thermal resistance of complex interfaces and promoting the practical application of micro–nano materials in the field of thermal management.

title: Engineering Tunable Helper Lipid Architecture to Improve Messenger RNA Lipid Nanoparticle Performance
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Helper lipids are essential structural components of lipid nanoparticles (LNPs), yet systematic design principles linking helper lipid architecture to messenger RNA (mRNA) delivery performance remain poorly defined. Here we identify helper lipid architecture as a major, largely unexplored design lever for optimizing LNP performance. Using a modular library of more than 80 rationally designed helper lipids, we show that systematic variation in headgroup chemistry, linker topology, and tail cardinality reshapes both LNP biophysical behavior and biological performance. Martini molecular dynamics (MD) simulations combined with multimodal structural analyses reveal that high‐performing scaffolds undergo a pH‐dependent transition into fusogenic inverse hexagonal‐like ordering, substantially lowering the energetic barrier for endosomal escape. These performance gains persist across the clinically relevant ALC‐0315 and DLin‐MC3‐DMA platforms, establishing helper lipid architecture as a transferable design parameter across distinct ionizable lipid chemistries. Translating these design principles into function, optimized helper lipid formulations restore hepatic protein expression in a mouse model of ornithine transcarbamylase (OTC) deficiency and increase antigen expression and immunogenicity in both preclinical models and in the in vitro human MIMIC platform. Together, these findings establish helper lipids as tunable molecular actuators of potency, tolerability, and stability, offering an engineering framework for next‐generation mRNA vaccines and therapeutics.

title: Privacy-Enhanced Federated Learning With Dynamic Reputation Consensus for Smart Grids
source: IEEE Transactions on Industrial Informatics
abstract: Smart-grid services increasingly rely on distributed learning, but pooling regional load records, operating parameters, and topology information can violate privacy and critical-infrastructure constraints. Federated learning avoids direct data sharing, yet local updates remain exposed to gradient inversion, protected aggregation limits the observability of Byzantine poisoning and free-riding behavior, and static blockchain trust can be strategically manipulated. This article proposes privacy-enhanced federated learning with dynamic reputation consensus for secure smart-grid collaboration. Its protected update path combines integral affine-bijective grouped encoding, participant-specific masking, Paillier aggregation, and Shamir-based mask recovery to reduce encrypted payloads, retain a masking layer after private-key exposure when masks remain unavailable, and tolerate participant dropout. A benchmark-model-driven Euclidean distance and cosine similarity audit converts complementary magnitude and directional evidence into cross-round reputation for validator and leader selection and deposit-based incentives. Experiments on heterogeneous image benchmarks and two real-world load-forecasting tasks show stable utility under non-IID data, independent, mixed, and delayed strategic poisoning, and dropout rates up to 30%. In the evaluated LeNet-5 configuration, the encrypted payload decreases from 812.19 MiB for parameterwise Paillier-FedAvg to 7.96 MiB per client per round. Under the evaluated attack conditions, the key-exposure test yields distorted reconstructions. The election tests show close agreement between empirical and theoretical leader-election probabilities.

title: DGSM-Net: Doppler-Guided Completion and Statistical Matching for 4-D Radar Odometry
source: IEEE Transactions on Industrial Informatics
abstract: Four-dimensional (4-D) millimeter-wave (mmWave) radar odometry has emerged as a promising alternative to vision- and LiDAR-based approaches due to its inherent robustness under adverse weather and illumination conditions. Nevertheless, 4-D radar point clouds are intrinsically sparse, geometrically ambiguous, and prone to spatial jump phenomena, which significantly degrade interframe registration reliability. To address these challenges, this article proposes DGSM-Net, a novel Doppler-guided and statistics-driven framework for robust 4-D radar odometry. Rather than treating Doppler measurements as ordinary auxiliary attributes or relying on deterministic feature matching, DGSM-Net uses Doppler-derived motion cues to guide geometric completion and models the matching process through local probabilistic inference under radar measurement uncertainty. First, to mitigate sparsity-induced geometric degradation, we develop a Doppler-guided geometric completion module, which aligns Doppler-derived motion cues with local geometric structures to enhance geometric completeness. Second, to alleviate spatial jump interference, we design a statistically guided robust matching module, which adopts NDT-based local probabilistic modeling and likelihood-guided confidence regulation to suppress unreliable correspondences. Extensive experiments on the public VoD benchmark, the self-collected dataset, and the long-range Snail-Radar dataset demonstrate that DGSM-Net achieves state-of-the-art odometry accuracy.

title: A Parallel Frequency Debiasing Network for Industrial Time Series Forecasting
source: IEEE Transactions on Industrial Informatics
abstract: Accurate forecasting of industrial time series is crucial for planning subsequent tasks and generating economic benefits. Existing methods often pay excessive attention to low-frequency components with high energy while neglecting high-frequency information that contains critical details, exhibiting frequency bias. These high-frequency components contain short-term trends and potential patterns. To address this challenge, we propose a parallel residual network with independent spectral modeling for industrial time series forecasting (PrismTS). PrismTS adopts a multistack parallel architecture, where each stack serves as an expert for a specific frequency band. These stacks independently model future spectra, utilizing an internal dual-residual structure for deep feature extraction. This parallel data-flow design enhances the sensitivity to weak high-frequency signals and improves computational efficiency. Each stack contains a block-shared frequency scale to adaptively select valuable frequencies and suppress noise in the corresponding band. The hierarchical supervision strategy imposes band-specific constraints on each stack, mitigating the cross-band bias of high-energy signals caused by the global loss. Each stack serves as a frequency interpolator that maps low-resolution spectra to high-resolution predictions within the same frequency band, achieving superresolution reconstruction in the frequency domain. By quantifying the output of each stack, the contributions of different frequency bands to the final forecast can be analyzed, which effectively enhances interpretability. Extensive experiments on multiple real-world datasets demonstrate that PrismTS achieves state-of-the-art accuracy and effectively mitigates frequency bias.

title: Magnetic Field Harmonic Modeling and Design of Fractional-Slot Dual-Winding Vernier PM Machines with Improved Torque and Power Factor
source: IEEE Transactions on Energy Conversion
abstract: In this paper, in order to further improve torque and power factor, a comprehensive magnetic field harmonic modeling and design approach is proposed for fractional-slot dual-winding vernier PM machine (FSDW-VPM). Firstly, analytical relationship among armature magnetic field harmonics, torque, and power factor is established. Then, the dominant armature harmonics contributing to torque and power factor characteristics are identified. Furthermore, to fully exploit dominant harmonics, the design concepts of dual-winding and hybrid-tooth are incorporated, enabling selective enhancement of dominant harmonics while suppressing those detrimental to the power factor. Finite element analysis (FEA) results show that the magnetic field harmonic modeling and design approach for synergistic harmonic improvement. Finally, a FSDW-VPM motor prototype is manufactured and tested to verify the effectiveness of the proposed method in improving the output torque and power factor.

title: Power Oscillation Suppression for Multi-Paralleled Grid-Forming Inverters via Hybrid Control
source: IEEE Transactions on Power Delivery
abstract: Grid-forming (GFM) inverters have grown ever more essential in power systems for their exceptional voltage and frequency support capabilities. However, due to the voltage based power regulation mechanism of traditional GFM controls, the active power regulation of multi-paralleled GFM inverters exhibits significant internal coupling, inducing undesirable power oscillation. Conventional control strategies such as increasing the virtual impedance for tackling this issue can partially suppress unfavorable interactions among multiple inverters but bring about negative effects including impairing voltage support capability. To overcome this limitation, this paper investigates the feasibility of suppressing power oscillation in grid-connected systems with multi-paralleled GFM inverters via a hybrid control based on current compensation, and further proposes targeted improvements with reference to the established active power loop coupling model. The proposed hybrid control scheme incorporates the advantages of current-based power regulation, and thus can effectively mitigate the power oscillation without compromising the closed-loop performance of the system. Finally, simulation and experimental results validate the effectiveness of the proposed scheme.
